# pets-eval toolkit map (generated by reader agents, verified by a critic)

Reference for the Mask benchmark adapter. Facts cite file:line in the supplied package. Verify against the code when in doubt.

## Critic corrections

- io.load_rowmap (toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:153-155): `original_record_id` is `.astype(str)` BEFORE `.dropna()`, so a blank/NaN original_record_id becomes the literal string "nan" and is kept; only rows whose protected_row fails `pd.to_numeric` are dropped. The scorecard map ('io load_rowmap') and attacks map ('Rowmap file contract') both say rows with NaN in either column are dropped. The adapter must never write blank ids (they would be matched against truth as 'nan' and silently miss).
- docs map 'CLI: text (leakage mode)' (docs/EVALUATION.md:49) under-specifies the command: toolkit/pets_eval/cli.py:68-74,127-134 require `--text-col COL` plus exactly one of `--id-col ID` or `--rowmap R`; omitting --text-col raises KeyError (df[None]); in the --rowmap branch --id-col is ignored and `values[rm.protected_row]` has no bounds check (cli.py:72) so a rowmap row >= len(df) raises IndexError. Unlike scorecard (scorecard.py:209 pops 'examples'), `pets-eval text` prints/writes the raw leaked PII values under 'examples' (text.py:131-132) - its output must not be exported.
- scorecard map 'cli detect' says the --pred CSV columns are undefined in scope: toolkit/pets_eval/detect.py:3-5 defines them as `dataset,table,column,privacy_role[,subtype]`; a missing key column raises ValueError (detect.py:31-32); catalog fields absent from the prediction are scored as role 'missing' (detect.py:41). Note io.load_catalog resolves the catalog from CWD via find_package_root (io.py:70) unless --root/--catalog is given.
- scorecard map gotcha 'If root cannot be found ... risks are empty, privacy is None and composite is None' is wrong: scorecard.py:88 writes `risks['direct identifiers retained'] = 0.0` unconditionally for every released table, even with an empty catalog, so privacy becomes 1.0 (a misleadingly perfect score), linkage/free-text/trajectory are silently skipped (scorecard.py:114,131,190 are guarded by `if root`), and no note is emitted (the `elif rm is None` at :185 does not fire when a rowmap exists). The adapter must always pass --root and assert the catalog resolved (e.g. k_anonymity has 'qis', not the 'no catalogued quasi-identifier kept' note, for customers).
- scorecard map 'risk 3': privacy.k_anonymity returns only {'qis','n':0} for an empty frame (privacy.py:33-34) and scorecard.py:107 then raises KeyError('share_below'); a released table with 0 rows and at least one catalogued QI kept therefore gets status 'error' (whole-table risks dropped), not an evaluation. None of the maps mention this.
- attacks map 'Risk 5: free-text identifier leakage' lists turns.text per-label counts (PERSON 19843, DATE 2837, 19 labels) as if they were the gold spans: the gold file metadata/pii_spans/customer_service__turns__text.jsonl has 20 labels (PERSON 19860, DATE 3018, AGE 527 ...); the listed numbers are scorecard `n` after text.py:121-123 drops spans whose normalised value is < 3 chars (all 2-digit AGE values, initials, short dates). So the leakage denominators are 48058/16751 for turns/agent_note, AGE can never contribute, and HEALTH/DATE/LOCATION/ORG/AGE are excluded from identifying_leakage_rate (text.py:19-21).
- docs map open question 'The --scenario flag appears mandatory': it is optional (cli.py:115); without it scorecard.py:248-260 runs all 7 CS tasks and marks every one required (None -> 0). With an unknown id, io.get_scenario returns None (io.py:84-88), the raw id string is stored under report['scenario'] and the same all-required behaviour applies (scorecard.py:294,301).
- scorecard map 'cli check': cmd_check prints masked examples (check.py:78-80) and never exits non-zero on hits; likewise cmd_scorecard exits 0 even when every table has status 'error' (errors are captured into the JSON at scorecard.py:310-311). The adapter must read `tables.*.status`, `linkage.*.evaluated`, `free_text.*.evaluated` and `utility[].metric` from scorecard.json rather than rely on exit codes.
- attacks map 'Linkage: function signature and early exits' and scorecard map 'risk 4': the stub for 'every attacker column this attack needs was removed' (scorecard.py:162-164) still triggers the baseline run on the ORIGINAL (scorecard.py:171-176, since res['evaluated'] is True), so the result carries baseline_reidentification_rate_original (0.8392 for CS) and risk_reduction 1.0 with qis_used=[] and n_targets_in_data=None; it is 'evaluated' with zero risk although no attack ran. Treat qis_used==[] as reduced coverage, not as a measured 0.
- text_utility map 'CS-U5 degradation' is incomplete: a duplicated turn_id in the protected turns makes `pt.set_index('turn_id').text.get(tid)` return a Series (customer_service.py:193,199) whose str() is tokenised as garbage (score drops, no error); and because the 20,000-turn sample (random_state=7) is drawn from ALL original turns including the eval split, withholding eval-split turns lowers CS-U5 proportionally. Duplicated conversation_id in protected conversations makes CS-U1's `reindex` raise (customer_service.py:126) -> metric 'error'.
- baselines map 'How baselines produce rowmaps' is right but the inference 'rowmap only meaningful when lengths match' is not a toolkit rule: scorecard.py:205-207 and attacks.py:415-418 accept any subset/reordering (out-of-range rows skipped, unmapped protected rows get person ''); verified by a scratch run where conversations was filtered to split=='train' and re-sorted with a rowmap: row_alignment 'row map', agent_note n_values 16751, k<5 scored, no error.
- scorecard map 'risk 6 synthetic' omits that dcr_report/membership_inference_auc sample rows with np.random.default_rng(0).choice over the PROTECTED frame (privacy.py:206-217,241-245), so for synthetic-branch tables with >20,000 (DCR) / >50,000 (MIA) rows the result depends on protected row order; for the row-level branch nothing depends on order except the rowmap indices.

No seed parameter exists on evaluate_table/run_scorecard; seeds are hard-wired (linkage seed=0 for adversary sampling only, dcr/MIA/trajectory seed=0, CS-U5 random_state=7, CS-U1 lbfgs deterministic) so runs are reproducible for identical inputs.
- Utility separately: `scorecard.run_utility('customer_service', orig_tables, prot_tables, scenario_dict)` (scorecard.py:246) or `t.fn(orig, prot)` from `pets_eval.utility.customer_service.TASKS`. Original-vs-protected answers are only exposed for CS-U1 (detail.f1_original/f1_protected) and CS-U2 (rho_original/rho_protected); CS-U3/U4/U6/U7 return only tvd/mape/mae and CS-U5 only `retained`. Programmatic: `text.redaction_leakage(io.load_spans(io.spans_path(root,'customer_service','turns','text')), {orig_turn_id: protected_text})`; CLI: `pets-eval text --gold metadata/pii_spans/customer_service__turns__text.jsonl --protected staging/customer_service/turns.csv --text-col text --rowmap staging/customer_service/rowmap_turns.csv`. The eval split (2962 conversations) has no public gold: leakage on eval rows is 'unsupported' locally (organiser-held), never 0. Records absent from the rowmap are skipped (treated as withheld) and reduce n_values - always report n_values next to the rate.

The linkage stub with qis_used=[] is 'evaluated' by the toolkit but should be flagged as zero-coverage.
- Representation-classification validation: after each run assert `tables[t].row_alignment == 'row map'` for every released row-level table; 'original record ids kept in the release (itself a linkage key)' means the record key leaked (scorecard.py:62-66, >50% of prot[rk] in original ids); 'none' means the table was scored as synthetic (k<5 unscored, linkage/free-text skipped, DCR+MIA vs holdout/customer_service/*.csv run instead - verified in a scratch run: customers with tokenised customer_id and no rowmap gave risks {direct ids 0.0, membership inference advantage 0.4212, exact copies 0.1554}).
- Sampling limits / denominators to record from config because the JSON does not state most of them: --max-adversary 3000 (CS adversary has 2600 rows, 2345 in-data targets, so no sampling), hash dictionary 300,000 candidates / 2,000,000 variants (scorecard.py:96, attacks.py:517), detect_hash_columns first 2000 non-null values (attacks.py:494), regex residual scan prot.head(20000) (scorecard.py:234), DCR 20,000 rows, MIA 5,000 per side and 50,000 synthetic (privacy.py:199,234,245), trajectory n_users=1000 (scorecard.py:120), CS-U5 20,000 original turns (customer_service.py:192). Reported counts: n_adversary_rows_tested, n_targets_in_data, n_values, per_label.n, k_anonymity.n, synthetic.dcr.n_synthetic, membership_inference.n_each.
- Score-composition gotcha: 'direct identifiers retained' is always present per released table (scorecard.py:88), and extra zero-valued components (e.g. a 64-hex HMAC pseudonym column triggers 'hashed ids reversible' = 0.0, attacks.py:490-500) lower the MEAN risk and raise the privacy score; conversely withholding a table removes all its components. Report the component set, not just the number.
- Export isolation specifics: never ship rowmap_*.csv, scorecard.json/html (absolute paths, scenario text, and `hash_attack.*.examples` holds raw reversed identifier values, attacks.py:542, not popped), `pets-eval text` output (raw examples), truth/, adversary/, holdout/, metadata/pii_spans/. `check` examples are masked (check.py:78-80). Because run_scorecard defaults out_dir to the protected folder (scorecard.py:319) and `check` rglobs .csv/.json inside the scanned folder (check.py:108), always pass --out to a separate directory and run `check` on the export folder, not the staging folder.
- Input-format hazards: io.read_table uses keep_default_na=True (io.py:49) so cells 'NA','N/A','NULL','null','NaN','nan','None','' become NaN -> wildcards in linkage (attacks.py:321-328) and dropped by _norm_vals; placeholder strings must not look like pandas NA tokens. Columns matching io.py:24-25 are forced to str, others inferred. CSVs must be RFC-quoted (turns.csv has 163,303 physical lines for 140,345 rows). Parquet is accepted for tables (io.py:45) but rowmaps are CSV-only (io.py:149). Extra staging files not named like an original table are listed in extra_protected_files and ignored; a stray file named like an original table is evaluated.
- Utility join-key requirements beyond `needs`: CS-U1 needs protected turns.conversation_id == protected conversations.conversation_id (a consistent pseudonym is fine) and either a protected `split` column or original conversation_id values (customer_service.py:122); CS-U5 needs turn_id kept verbatim (pseudonymised turn_id -> score ~0, not 'not answerable'); withholding eval-split rows does not hurt CS-U1 (tests on original eval docs) or free-text leakage (train-only gold) but hurts CS-U5. CS-U7 treats anything outside {'true','1','yes'} as unresolved; CS-U2 uses pd.to_numeric on csat (ranges -> NaN -> hard 0.0).
- Running environment: `pets-eval` is not installed; verified invocation is `cd <PKG> && PYTHONPATH=<PKG>/toolkit python3 -m pets_eval ...` (python 3.12.3, numpy 2.4.6, pandas 2.3.3, scipy 1.17.1, scikit-learn 1.9.0 present). Full CS scorecard takes ~8-30 s. Record pets_eval.__version__ ('1.0.0'), a hash of toolkit/pets_eval, metadata/attack_specs.json (version '1.0'), metadata/field_catalog.csv, metadata/scenarios.json and the pii_spans files with every result; PETS_ROOT env var is an alternative to --root (io.py:30-32).
- Coverage gaps the adapter must display as not covered (not as 0): only customers has a linkage spec (conversations/turns get the 'no attack spec' note); no trajectory, no cross-table (customer_id/started_ts) attack, no eval-split text gold, no hidden-attacker results (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md:32-42, docs/EVALUATION.md:51-63 pets_submission/ layout is for future organiser checks); regex_residuals is informational only and never enters the score (scorecard.py:232-241); social_checkins/vacation_posts are not auto-scored (THREAT_MODEL.md:30, not CS).
- Span-prediction path for a redactor that emits spans: `pets-eval text --gold ... --pred spans.jsonl` with one JSON per line {record_id, spans:[{start,end,label}]} where offsets are into the ORIGINAL text; result has 'exact', 'overlap', 'overlap_label_agnostic' (text.py:37-74); `text.spans_from_redaction(original, protected)` (text.py:149-158) recovers 'ANY' spans by difflib. pets_eval.utility.customer_service.span_scores/leak_rate are a second, non-identical implementation (no one-to-one matching, verbatim lower-case, min_len 4, missing records count as empty) - state which one is reported.
- Attribute inference on accessibility_needs: values are compared as str so NaN -> 'nan' (attacks.py:434); with 97% empty in the original, homogeneous candidate sets of 'nan' count as correct inferences but the majority base rate cancels this in advantage_over_base_rate (attacks.py:473-482); report success_rate with base_rate, not alone. The component 'linkage re-identification' is max(reidentification_rate, advantage_over_base_rate).

Originals: PKG/data/customer_service/{customers,conversations,turns}.csv (9591/11943/140345 rows). Catalog roles: customers record_key=customer_id, direct_identifier={customer_number,full_name,hetu,street_address,email,phone,contract_number,iban}, quasi={postcode,city,preferred_language,customer_since}, sensitive={payment_default_flag,accessibility_needs}; conversations record_key=conversation_id, technical={customer_id,agent_id}, direct={agent_name}, quasi={language,started_ts}, free_text=agent_note; turns record_key=turn_id, technical=conversation_id, quasi=ts, free_text=text.

STAGING LAYOUT (private, written by the TypeScript plan executor; never exported):
<run>/staging/customer_service/customers.csv        # same file name, original column names for kept columns, generalised values allowed ('201**', '30-39', '2025-W12', '2025-03', 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:00'); new columns allowed (listed as columns_added); do NOT emit 'NA'/'null'/'nan'/'None'/'' as placeholder values
<run>/staging/customer_service/conversations.csv
<run>/staging/customer_service/turns.csv             # RFC-4180 quoted multi-line text; omit a file entirely to withhold the table
<run>/staging/customer_service/rowmap_customers.csv  # header exactly: protected_row,original_record_id ; protected_row = 0-based DataFrame row index of the protected CSV AFTER all filtering/sorting/suppression; original_record_id = original customer_id string (C000001); omit rows for suppressed/synthetic records; never blank ids; no duplicates of protected_row
<run>/staging/customer_service/rowmap_conversations.csv  # original_record_id = conversation_id (CNV-000001)
<run>/staging/customer_service/rowmap_turns.csv          # original_record_id = turn_id (T0000001)
<run>/out/                                           # scorecard.json + scorecard.html go here (never into staging)
<run>/export/customer_service/*.csv                  # shareable artifact = staging tables only; no rowmap_*, no scorecard.*, no text-leakage JSON, no truth/adversary/holdout/pii_spans
Rules: a released row-level table MUST have its rowmap (else the toolkit scores it as synthetic and skips linkage, free-text leakage and k<5); files whose stem starts with 'rowmap_' or '_' are not tables; pseudonymised conversation_id must be identical across conversations.csv and turns.csv and conversations.split should be kept (CS-U1); turn_id should be kept verbatim if CS-U5 matters; record-key columns kept verbatim trigger row_alignment 'original record ids kept in the release (itself a linkage key)'.

COMMANDS (Python runner; run from PKG so find_package_root works, and still pass --root):

python3 -m pets_eval scenarios --dataset customer_service --root $PKG
python3 -m pets_eval tasks --dataset customer_service
python3 -m pets_eval scorecard --original $PKG/data/customer_service --protected <run>/staging/customer_service --scenario CS-S1 --root $PKG --out <run>/out --max-adversary 3000      # CS-S1|CS-S2|CS-S3; omit --scenario to run all 7 tasks as required
python3 -m pets_eval check <run>/export/customer_service --out <run>/out/check.json           # residual regex scan of the EXPORT (masked examples); informational
python3 -m pets_eval text --gold $PKG/metadata/pii_spans/customer_service__turns__text.jsonl --protected <run>/staging/customer_service/turns.csv --text-col text --rowmap <run>/staging/customer_service/rowmap_turns.csv --out <run>/out/leak_turns.json              # optional standalone; output contains raw leaked values, keep private
python3 -m pets_eval text --gold $PKG/metadata/pii_spans/customer_service__conversations__agent_note.jsonl --protected <run>/staging/customer_service/conversations.csv --text-col agent_note --rowmap <run>/staging/customer_service/rowmap_conversations.csv --out <run>/out/leak_notes.json
Programmatic equivalents: scorecard.run_scorecard(original_dir, protected_dir, scenario='CS-S1', root=PKG, rowmaps=None, out_dir=<run>/out, max_adversary=3000) -> dict; scorecard.evaluate_table(domain, table, orig_df, prot_df, cat, root, scenario_dict, rowmap_df, max_adversary); scorecard.run_utility(domain, orig_tables, prot_tables, scenario_dict); attacks.linkage_attack(adv, truth, prot, rowmap, identity, qis=attacks.qis_from_spec(spec['qis'], prot.columns), original=orig, record_key='customer_id', sensitive='accessibility_needs', max_adversary=3000, seed=0); text.redaction_leakage(gold, {original_record_id: protected_text}).

READ FROM <run>/out/scorecard.json: tool, dataset, scenario (dict or raw id), tables.<t>.status in {released, withheld, error}, tables.<t>.row_alignment in {'row map', 'original record ids kept in the release (itself a linkage key)', 'none'} (assert 'row map' for every released row-level table), tables.<t>.risks {direct identifiers retained (always), hashed ids reversible, records with k<5, linkage re-identification, free-text identifier leakage, membership inference advantage, exact copies of original rows}, tables.customers.linkage.leaked_customer_list {evaluated, qis_used, n_adversary_rows_tested, n_targets_in_data, reidentification_rate, claim_precision, n_unique_claims, share_targets_in_candidate_set_le5, median_candidate_set, attribute_inference{...}, baseline_reidentification_rate_original, risk_reduction} (conversations/turns carry linkage.note 'no attack spec targets this table'), tables.conversations.free_text.agent_note and tables.turns.free_text.text {evaluated, leakage_rate, leakage_rate_chars, identifying_leakage_rate, per_label{label:{n,leaked,rate}}, n_values} or {evaluated:false, reason} or {evaluated:true, status:'withheld', identifying_leakage_rate:0.0}, tables.<t>.k_anonymity {qis,n,n_classes,min_k,median_k,share_below{k<2,k<5,k<10},sample_uniqueness[,note]}, regex_residuals (informational), utility[] {id, table, kind, description, required, score|null, metric, detail}, summary {privacy, utility, composite, label, method}, risk_components {'<table>: <name>': float}. Status mapping: evaluated = component present / evaluated:true / score not null; not_applicable = withheld table, 'no attack spec targets this table', free_text status 'withheld', k<5 popped for synthetic; unsupported = evaluated:false with reason, metric 'not answerable' (detail.missing), eval-split text (no public gold), root/catalog unresolved; failed = status 'error', reason 'error: ...', metric 'error'. Exit code is 0 in all these cases. Record with each result: scenario id, toolkit version + file hashes (toolkit dir, attack_specs.json, field_catalog.csv, scenarios.json, pii_spans), plan/input/output hashes, max_adversary and the fixed sampling limits (hash 300k/2M, regex head 20000, DCR 20000, MIA 5000/side, CS-U5 20000 turns, seeds 0 / random_state 7), and denominators (n_targets_in_data 2345 of 2600, n_values per text column, k_anonymity.n).

## Reader: docs

Mapped the five pets-eval docs. The toolkit is a self-assessment CLI (`pets-eval`) plus Python API (`pets_eval.privacy/attacks/text/detect/parse/utility`). The adapter must write a protected folder that mirrors the original dataset folder (same table file names, original column names, generalised values allowed) plus a private `rowmap_<table>.csv` (`protected_row`,`original_record_id`) per released row-level table; a table with neither a rowmap nor original record ids is scored as synthetic (DCR + membership inference vs `holdout/`), and an absent table is reported as withheld. Scorecard privacy = 1 − (0.5·worst risk + 0.5·mean risk) over seven risk components; utility = mean of the scenario's required tasks (unanswerable required task = 0); composite = weighted harmonic mean (privacy 30, utility 25). Customer_service attacker is `leaked_customer_list.csv` (names/emails/phones found in transcripts and redacted text), and customer_service baseline scores are B0/B2/B2-k privacy 0.22/0.31/0.50, utility 1.00/0.86/0.86, worst re-id 0.00/0.00/0.00; CS-S1 1.00/0.75/0.75, CS-S2 1.00/0.66/0.66, CS-S3 1.00/1.00/1.00. The docs give CLI commands but no function signatures, no JSON output schema, no per-test status vocabulary, and no sampling limits; these are open questions that require reading `toolkit/pets_eval/` source, `metadata/attack_specs.json`, `metadata/field_catalog.csv`, `results/`, and `baselines/run_all.py`.

- **CLI: install**: Install with `pip install -e ./toolkit` or `export PYTHONPATH=$PWD/toolkit`. _(toolkit/README.md:8)_
- **CLI: scenarios**: `pets-eval scenarios` lists sharing scenarios (no flags documented). _(toolkit/README.md:9)_
- **CLI: tasks**: `pets-eval tasks --dataset health` lists utility tasks for a dataset; flag `--dataset <name>`. _(toolkit/README.md:10; docs/EVALUATION.md:38)_
- **CLI: check**: `pets-eval check my_out/` scans a protected output folder for residual direct identifiers: HETU, IBAN, cards, e-mail, phones, IPs, MACs, plates. Positional argument is the output folder. _(toolkit/README.md:11)_
- **CLI: detect**: `pets-eval detect --pred my_field_labels.csv` scores a prediction CSV with columns `dataset,table,column,privacy_role,subtype` against `metadata/field_catalog.csv`; reports per-role precision/recall/F1, macro-F1, subtype accuracy and a confusion matrix. _(toolkit/README.md:12; docs/EVALUATION.md:46)_
- **CLI: text (span mode)**: `pets-eval text --gold <spans.jsonl> --pred <my_spans.jsonl>` reports span precision, recall and F2 per label (F2 weights recall higher). Example gold path: `metadata/pii_spans/customer_service__turns__text.jsonl`. _(toolkit/README.md:13; docs/EVALUATION.md:48)_
- **CLI: text (leakage mode)**: `pets-eval text --gold <spans.jsonl> --protected <redacted.csv>` checks which gold PII values survive in redacted text, independent of redaction style. This is the free-text leakage check for an adapter that redacts rather than labels spans. _(docs/EVALUATION.md:49)_
- **CLI: scorecard**: `pets-eval scorecard --original data/health --protected my_out/health --scenario HEALTH-S1`. Flags: `--original <dataset folder>`, `--protected <protected folder>`, `--scenario <SCENARIO-ID>`. Runs linkage attacks from `metadata/attack_specs.json` and trajectory unicity for mobility/smart-city tables. _(toolkit/README.md:14; docs/THREAT_MODEL.md:28)_
- **Span file semantics**: In span JSONL files, a record absent from the file, or present with an empty `spans` list, contains no labelled PII. _(docs/EVALUATION.md:47)_
- **Output folder: table naming**: Protected folder must use the same table file names as the original (e.g. `ed_visits.csv`); a table not released is reported as withheld. _(docs/EVALUATION.md:7; toolkit/README.md:18)_
- **Output folder: column naming and generalised values**: Keep original column names for kept columns. Accepted generalised forms: ages `30-39`, `90+`; postcodes `201**`, `201`; times rounded, `2025-03`, `2025-W12`; coordinates rounded; ICD-10 3-character codes or diagnosis groups. _(docs/EVALUATION.md:8-16; toolkit/README.md:19-20)_
- **Output folder: rowmap**: For each released row-level (microdata) table add `rowmap_<table>.csv` with columns `protected_row` (0-based row index into the protected table) and `original_record_id`. Used only for scoring; must never be published. _(docs/EVALUATION.md:18; toolkit/README.md:21-22)_
- **Classification branch: row-level vs synthetic**: A table with neither a row map nor original record ids is evaluated as synthetic data, using distance to closest record (DCR/NNDR) and membership inference against `holdout/`. Presence of a rowmap OR original record ids keeps it in row-level evaluation. _(docs/EVALUATION.md:19; toolkit/README.md:23-24)_
- **Output folder: DP answers**: To answer the health DP workload, add `dp_answers.csv` with columns `id,value` and describe the mechanism (ε, δ, unit of privacy, contribution bound). Health-only; B3 workload has 254 queries. _(docs/EVALUATION.md:20; docs/BENCHMARK.md:76)_
- **Privacy component: direct identifiers retained**: Share of values of catalogued direct identifiers that still appear verbatim (0 = none, 1 = maximal). _(docs/EVALUATION.md:26)_
- **Privacy component: hashed ids reversible**: Share of hashed values recovered by hashing candidate values with unsalted MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256 (hash dictionary attack). _(docs/EVALUATION.md:27; toolkit/README.md:28)_
- **Privacy component: records with k<5**: Share of rows in equivalence classes smaller than 5 on the catalogued quasi-identifiers that were kept. _(docs/EVALUATION.md:28)_
- **Privacy component: linkage re-identification**: Worst re-identification or attribute-inference rate over the attacks defined in `metadata/attack_specs.json`. Worst re-id = highest share of attacker targets singled out by any attack, or attribute-inference advantage over guessing, whichever is higher. _(docs/EVALUATION.md:29; docs/BENCHMARK.md:16)_
- **Privacy component: free-text identifier leakage**: Share of gold PII spans whose value survives in the protected text. _(docs/EVALUATION.md:30)_
- **Privacy component: trajectory unicity**: Share of subjects (cards, accounts, devices, vehicles) singled out by a few known (place, hour) points, for tables listed under `trajectories` in `attack_specs.json`. In original taps 4 points single out ~98% of cards. _(docs/EVALUATION.md:31; docs/THREAT_MODEL.md:28)_
- **Privacy component: synthetic DCR / membership inference**: For synthetic tables: rows copied from the original (exact copies / DCR) and advantage of a membership attacker over a coin flip. B4 reports components named 'membership inference advantage' and 'exact copies of original rows'. _(docs/EVALUATION.md:32; docs/BENCHMARK.md:94-95)_
- **Privacy score formula**: privacy = 1 − (0.5 × worst risk + 0.5 × mean risk) over the risk components. _(docs/EVALUATION.md:34; docs/BENCHMARK.md:16)_
- **Utility score**: Each dataset has 6–11 utility tasks. Each task asks the same question of original and protected data and scores agreement in [0,1]. A task that cannot be answered (needed column removed/coarsened) is 'not answerable' and scores 0 when the chosen scenario requires it. Utility = mean over the scenario's tasks. _(docs/EVALUATION.md:38)_
- **Composite score**: Composite = weighted harmonic mean of privacy (weight 30) and utility (weight 25). _(docs/EVALUATION.md:42)_
- **Attacker model: general capabilities**: Attacker knows schema and published method (Kerckhoffs), not secret keys/seeds; can hash candidate emails/HETUs/phones and compare; can combine every public file in the package; cannot access original data. _(docs/THREAT_MODEL.md:46-49)_
- **Attacker model: success criteria**: Success = (1) re-identification: correct unique match attacker row → protected record; (2) attribute inference with confidence clearly above base rate; (3) membership inference (synthetic) better than chance; (4) residual direct identifiers anywhere, including inside free text. _(docs/THREAT_MODEL.md:53-56)_
- **Attacker model: customer_service**: `adversary/leaked_customer_list.csv` (an old marketing list) holds names, emails, phones; typical attack: find customers in transcripts and redacted text. Truth file at `truth/adversary__leaked_customer_list.csv`. _(docs/THREAT_MODEL.md:24,26)_
- **Attacker model: per-dataset files**: public_directory.csv (name/address/postcode/city/phone → link to postcode+age+sex); news_clips_health.csv & social_posts_health.csv (ED visit); social_checkins.csv & fitness_app_leak.csv (trajectory linkage to transit/bike); plate_sightings.csv (ANPR parking); vacation_posts.csv (empty home in meter data); receipt_photos_ocr.csv (card last4/time/merchant/amount → card transactions); company_website_staff.csv (reverse pseudonymised users/hostnames/hashed emails); sports_club_rosters.csv & graduation_lists.csv (students); neighbourhood_forum_posts.csv (service requests). _(docs/THREAT_MODEL.md:13-24)_
- **Attacks not auto-scored**: `social_checkins.csv` (needs stop-name join) and `vacation_posts.csv` (attribute-inference on meter data) are not scored automatically by scorecard. _(docs/THREAT_MODEL.md:30)_
- **Hidden attackers**: Organisers hold a private stronger attacker set per domain: data-broker profile, HR sick-leave knowledge, colleague commute knowledge, merchant card-number view, municipal insider. Not in package. _(docs/THREAT_MODEL.md:34-42; docs/EVALUATION.md:55)_
- **Baseline definitions**: B0 drops catalogued direct identifiers, keeps everything else. B1 rule-based field detector (column names + value patterns). B2 classic SDC: keyed HMAC pseudonyms, prefix-preserving IPs, birth year not date, 10-year age bands, 3-digit postcodes, coords at 2 decimals, timestamps to the hour, regex redaction of free text. B2-k = B2 + local suppression until every row has k≥5 on catalogued QIs. B3 person-level Laplace DP on health query workload. B4 synthetic ED visits from a chain Bayesian network. Baselines read the field catalog rather than detecting fields. _(docs/BENCHMARK.md:3,7-12)_
- **Baseline provenance**: All baseline numbers come from `python3 baselines/run_all.py` with pets-eval 1.0.0; scorecards stored in `results/`. _(docs/BENCHMARK.md:3)_
- **customer_service baseline scores**: Privacy B0/B2/B2-k = 0.22/0.31/0.50; Utility (all tasks) = 1.00/0.86/0.86; Worst re-identification = 0.00/0.00/0.00. _(docs/BENCHMARK.md:28)_
- **customer_service scenario utility**: CS-S1: 1.00/0.75/0.75; CS-S2: 1.00/0.66/0.66; CS-S3: 1.00/1.00/1.00 (B0/B2/B2-k). _(docs/BENCHMARK.md:58-60)_
- **B1 detection scores**: Macro-F1 over privacy roles 0.65; recall of sensitive columns 0.73. Roles: direct_identifier, quasi_identifier, sensitive_attribute, technical_identifier, free_text, record_key, non_sensitive. _(docs/BENCHMARK.md:64-74)_
- **B3 DP scores**: Each patient contributes ≤4 visits; ε split over 5 query families; utility = 1 − mean relative error / 0.5. ε 0.25→0.24, 0.5→0.50, 1.0→0.69, 2.0→0.80, 5.0→0.87. _(docs/BENCHMARK.md:78-86)_
- **B4 synthetic scores**: Privacy 1.00, utility 0.38, composite 0.57; components: direct identifiers retained 0, free-text leakage 0, membership inference advantage 0, exact copies 0; utility tasks H-U2 0.05, H-U3 0.29, H-U5 0.79. _(docs/BENCHMARK.md:90-101)_
- **Baseline lessons**: B0 still leaks 79% of card-transaction targets via receipts (date,time,amount); B2 generalisation without k check leaves most rows unique; keyed pseudonyms preserve joins (cyber detections, revisit analyses) while random tokens/dropped keys break them; regex redaction misses names, spoken numbers and spelled-out emails. _(docs/BENCHMARK.md:105-109)_
- **Python API modules**: `pets_eval.privacy` (k-anonymity, l-diversity, t-closeness, uniqueness, small cells, differencing, DCR/NNDR, membership inference, trajectory unicity); `pets_eval.attacks` (linkage attack, attribute inference, hash dictionary attack, HETU enumeration); `pets_eval.text`; `pets_eval.detect`; `pets_eval.parse`; `pets_eval.utility`. _(toolkit/README.md:26-29)_
- **Organiser submission folder**: For optional organiser checks put outputs in `pets_submission/`: `unseen_field_labels.csv`; `customer_service_eval_redacted.csv` (`turn_id,text`) or `customer_service_eval_spans.jsonl`; protected tables with row maps, one subfolder per dataset. Unseen dataset is `data/unseen/export_2025_q4.csv`. _(docs/EVALUATION.md:56-63)_
- **Data properties**: One synthetic population of 100,000 residents in real Southwest Finland postcode areas; same people appear across datasets (mosaic effect). HETUs use 900–999 temporary range, IBANs non-Finnish bank id, cards public test BINs, emails `.example` domains. _(docs/THREAT_MODEL.md:7-9; docs/LIMITATIONS.md:10)_
- **Free text generation**: Notes, chats and complaints are template-generated with variation and noise; detectors that overfit templates do worse on real text. _(docs/LIMITATIONS.md:7)_
- **Toolkit location**: Toolkit source lives in `toolkit/pets_eval/` with `toolkit/pyproject.toml`; licence MIT. _(ls of toolkit/; toolkit/README.md:31)_

Gotchas:
- The rowmap uses `protected_row` as a 0-based index into the protected CSV, so any row reordering, filtering or suppression in the Mask plan must be reflected when writing the map; dropped rows simply have no map entry (docs/EVALUATION.md:18).
- Omitting the rowmap AND removing original record ids silently flips a table into synthetic evaluation (DCR + membership inference against holdout/), which changes the component set and the score (docs/EVALUATION.md:19). Keep either one if row-level scoring is intended.
- Tables missing from the protected folder are 'withheld', not failed; the docs do not say how withheld tables affect utility tasks that need them (likely 'not answerable' = 0 if required by scenario) (docs/EVALUATION.md:7,38).
- Privacy score punishes the single worst component at 50% weight, so one residual identifier column or a reversible unsalted hash dominates the score (docs/EVALUATION.md:34).
- Hashed ids are tested by unsalted MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256 dictionary attack; HMAC/keyed pseudonyms are what the B2 baseline uses to survive it (docs/EVALUATION.md:27; docs/BENCHMARK.md:9).
- Generalised values must stay in the accepted forms (`30-39`, `201**`, `2025-W12`, etc.) under the original column names or the parser may not understand them (docs/EVALUATION.md:10-16).
- Free-text leakage is scored by whether gold span values survive in redacted text (`--protected`), independent of redaction style; regex-only redaction misses names, spoken numbers, spelled-out emails (docs/EVALUATION.md:49; docs/BENCHMARK.md:108).
- Two shipped attacker files (social_checkins.csv, vacation_posts.csv) are not scored by scorecard; an adapter should not report them as evaluated (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md:30).
- `pets-eval check` is a separate residual-identifier scan from the scorecard's 'direct identifiers retained' component; both exist (toolkit/README.md:11; docs/EVALUATION.md:26).
- Baselines read the field catalog instead of detecting fields, so their numbers reflect protection alone and are not directly comparable to a pipeline that also detects (docs/BENCHMARK.md:3).
- DP answers (`dp_answers.csv`) are only relevant to the health workload; non-health datasets have no DP file convention in the docs (docs/EVALUATION.md:20).

Open questions:
- Exact Python function signatures in pets_eval.privacy / attacks / text / detect / parse / utility are not in the docs; need to read toolkit/pets_eval/*.py.
- The JSON (or other) output structure of `pets-eval scorecard`, `check`, `text` and `detect` is not documented; need to inspect the CLI source and the sample scorecards under results/.
- No per-test status vocabulary (evaluated / not_applicable / unsupported / failed) exists in the docs; the adapter will have to define it from the toolkit's behaviour.
- Sampling limits, row caps or subsampling for attacks, DCR or membership inference are not mentioned in the docs; check attack_specs.json and the source.
- Denominators for each component (e.g. number of attacker targets, number of gold spans, number of catalogued direct-identifier values) are implied but not spelled out; need source.
- What 'original record ids' means concretely (which column name the scorecard looks for, e.g. record_key role from field_catalog.csv) is not stated in the docs.
- Whether `pets-eval scorecard` can score a single table or dataset subset, or how it handles extra/unknown files in the protected folder, is not documented.
- Whether `pets-eval text --protected` accepts the full protected turns CSV or requires the `turn_id,text` layout mentioned for the organiser submission is not stated.
- The exact per-dataset attack list, join keys and `trajectories` table list live in metadata/attack_specs.json, not in the docs.
- Which utility tasks each customer_service scenario (CS-S1/S2/S3) requires is in docs/SCENARIOS.md and `pets-eval tasks --dataset customer_service`, not in the five files read.
- How a withheld table affects utility tasks that depend on it (0 vs skipped) is not specified.
- The `--scenario` flag appears mandatory in the example; whether scorecard runs without it (all tasks) is not stated.
- Exit codes and failure modes of the CLI (e.g. malformed rowmap, missing holdout/) are undocumented.
- The pets-eval version pinned in toolkit/pyproject.toml vs the 1.0.0 used for baselines should be confirmed.

## Reader: scorecard

pets-eval 1.0.0 is a Python >=3.10 package (numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn) exposing `pets-eval <cmd>` (entry point pets_eval.cli:main; also `python -m pets_eval`). The scorecard command loads original and protected folders as {table_stem: DataFrame} (every *.csv/*.parquet, skipping rowmap_* and _* files), auto-discovers rowmap_<table>.csv in the protected folder, and per original table marks it `withheld` (not in protected folder), `released` (evaluated) or `error`. Row alignment (`row_alignment`) is decided by `_record_ids_for_rows`: an explicit rowmap wins ("row map"); otherwise if the record-key column is kept and >50% of its values are original ids the table is auto-aligned ("original record ids kept in the release (itself a linkage key)"); otherwise `rm is None` and the table is treated as synthetic/aggregate: k<5 risk is dropped from scoring, linkage is not evaluated, free text is not evaluated (reason "needs a row map to align texts"), and DCR / membership-inference run instead. Risk components are flat strings keyed "<table>: <risk name>"; privacy = 1-(0.5*max+0.5*mean), utility = mean of task scores with required-but-None scored 0 and optional-None excluded, composite = weighted harmonic mean (30/25). Output: <out>/scorecard.json and scorecard.html. The attack/privacy/text/check/utility internals (seeds, sampling, metric names, task registry, catalog columns beyond those referenced) live in files not in scope and are listed as open questions.

- **package**: Package name pets-eval, version 1.0.0, requires-python >=3.10, dependencies numpy>=1.24, pandas>=2.0, scipy>=1.10, scikit-learn>=1.2; console script `pets-eval = pets_eval.cli:main`; setuptools finds packages `pets_eval*`. _(toolkit/pyproject.toml:6-19)_
- **package**: `python -m pets_eval` runs cli.main() (toolkit/pets_eval/__main__.py:1-3). Package modules present: __init__, attacks, check, cli, detect, io, parse, privacy, scorecard, text, utility/ (directory). _(toolkit/pets_eval/__main__.py:1-3; ls toolkit/pets_eval)_
- **cli**: Subcommands (argparse, dest=cmd, required): scorecard, detect, text, check, tasks, scenarios. _(toolkit/pets_eval/cli.py:108-147)_
- **cli scorecard**: `pets-eval scorecard --original DIR --protected DIR [--rowmap CSV|table=path ...(append)] [--scenario ID] [--root PKG_ROOT] [--out DIR] [--max-adversary N (int, default 3000)]`. --original and --protected required. Help text: rowmap auto-detected as rowmap_<table>.csv; --out defaults to protected folder. _(toolkit/pets_eval/cli.py:111-119)_
- **cli scorecard**: cmd_scorecard parses --rowmap values: if value contains '=' it is split once into table=path, else table = Path(value).stem with 'rowmap_' removed (str.replace, so any occurrence) and path = value. Then calls scorecard.run_scorecard(a.original, a.protected, a.scenario, a.root, rowmaps, a.out, a.max_adversary). _(toolkit/pets_eval/cli.py:26-35)_
- **cli scorecard**: Stdout after run: line `privacy {p}  utility {u}  composite {c}  ({label})`, then one `  risk  {v:6.1%}  {k}` per risk_components entry, one `  util  {score:.2f|'n/a '}  {id}  {metric}` per utility task, then `wrote {out}/scorecard.json and {out}/scorecard.html` where out = Path(a.out or a.protected). _(toolkit/pets_eval/cli.py:36-44)_
- **cli detect**: `pets-eval detect --pred CSV [--catalog CSV] [--root R] [--datasets a,b] [--out JSON]`. Loads catalog via io.load_catalog(root, catalog), reads --pred with pd.read_csv(dtype=str), calls detect.score_detection(pred, cat, datasets_list_or_None); writes full result JSON to --out, then pops 'errors' and 'confusion' keys before printing to stdout. Column names of the pred CSV are not defined in these files. _(toolkit/pets_eval/cli.py:47-55,120-126)_
- **cli text**: `pets-eval text --gold metadata/pii_spans/<domain>__<table>__<column>.jsonl (--pred spans.jsonl | --protected file.csv --text-col COL (--id-col ID | --rowmap R)) [--out JSON]`. With --pred: result = {"exact": span_scores(gold,pred,'exact'), "overlap": span_scores(gold,pred,'overlap'), "overlap_label_agnostic": span_scores(gold,pred,'overlap',label_agnostic=True)}. With --protected: table read with io.read_table; if --rowmap, texts = {original_record_id: df[text_col].fillna('').astype(str).values[protected_row]} (positional index, no bounds check), else texts = {str(df[id_col]): text}; result = text.redaction_leakage(gold, texts). Neither given -> sys.exit with usage message. _(toolkit/pets_eval/cli.py:62-80,127-135)_
- **cli check**: `pets-eval check PATH [--max-lines N] [--out JSON]` calls check.scan_path(path, max_lines); report keys used: n_files_scanned, totals (dict kind->count), examples (dict kind->list[str]), note. Prints `scanned N files`, then per kind sorted by count desc `  {kind:15s} {count:8d}  e.g. ...`, or 'no residual direct identifiers found by the regex scan' when totals empty, then rep['note']. _(toolkit/pets_eval/cli.py:83-92,136-140)_
- **cli tasks**: `pets-eval tasks [--dataset D]` imports pets_eval.utility.all_tasks and prints `{t.id:28s} {t.dataset:16s} {t.table:22s} {t.description}` for all_tasks([dataset] if dataset else None). Task objects have attributes id, dataset, table, description, kind, scenarios, fn (see scorecard.run_utility). _(toolkit/pets_eval/cli.py:95-98,141-143; scorecard.py:247-260)_
- **cli scenarios**: `pets-eval scenarios [--dataset D] [--root R]` iterates io.load_scenarios(root), filters s.get('dataset') == dataset, prints `{id:14s} {trust_level:20s} {title}`. Scenario dict keys referenced across files: id, dataset, trust_level, title, threat_model, utility_requirements. _(toolkit/pets_eval/cli.py:101-105,144-147; scorecard.py:50,248,250)_
- **io package layout**: Documented package layout: data/<domain>/<table>.csv (originals); metadata/field_catalog.csv (dataset, table, column, privacy_role, subtype, ...); metadata/scenarios.json; metadata/pii_spans/<domain>__<table>__<column>.jsonl; adversary/<name>.csv; truth/adversary__<name>.csv (adv_row_id -> person_id); truth/<domain>__<table>.csv (record_id -> person_id); holdout/<domain>/<table>.csv (non-member records for MIA). _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:3-11)_
- **io find_package_root**: find_package_root(start=None): if env PETS_ROOT set and <PETS_ROOT>/metadata exists -> that path resolved; else walk from start (or CWD; a file path uses its parent) upward and return the first dir where metadata/ is a dir and (data/ or adversary/) is a dir; else None. _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:28-39)_
- **io read_table dtype**: read_table(path): .parquet -> pd.read_parquet; CSV -> header read first, then columns whose name matches regex `(^|_)(id|ids|hetu|ssn|postcode|zip|phone|mobile|iban|pan|card|plate|gsrn|meter|mac|imei|ip|code|icd|number|no|account|msisdn|ref|reference|property)($|_)|_id$|^id_` (case-insensitive) are forced to dtype str; other columns inferred; low_memory=False, keep_default_na=True (so empty strings become NaN). _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:23-25,42-49)_
- **io load_tables**: load_tables(folder, tables=None) -> {stem: DataFrame} over sorted(folder/*.csv + folder/*.parquet); skips stems starting with 'rowmap_' or '_'; optional whitelist `tables`; returns {} if folder missing. Table name = file stem, so protected file must be named <table>.csv (or .parquet) exactly like the original. _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:52-65)_
- **io load_catalog**: load_catalog(root=None, path=None): path defaults to <root or find_package_root() or '.'>/metadata/field_catalog.csv; read with dtype=str and fillna(''); if column art9_special_category present it is converted to bool (lower in {'true','1','yes'}). Catalog columns used by scorecard: dataset, table, column, privacy_role, data_kind; roles referenced: record_key, direct_identifier, technical_identifier, quasi_identifier, sensitive_attribute, free_text; data_kind value 'temporal'. _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:68-75; scorecard.py:36-39,80,93,101-102,138,161,189,217-218,291-292)_
- **io scenarios**: load_scenarios(root) reads <root>/metadata/scenarios.json as a JSON list (returns [] if absent); get_scenario(id, root) returns the first dict with s['id']==id else None. _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:78-88)_
- **io spans**: spans_path(root, domain, table, column) = <root>/metadata/pii_spans/<domain>__<table>__<column>.jsonl. load_spans(path) -> {str(record_id): spans list} where each JSONL line is {record_id, spans:[{start,end,label,text},...]} (spans defaults to []); raises FileNotFoundError if missing. list_span_files(root, domain=None) -> [(domain, table, column, path)] for stems with exactly 3 '__'-separated parts. _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:91-119)_
- **io adversary/truth/holdout**: list_adversaries(root) = sorted stems of <root>/adversary/*.csv. load_adversary(root, name) -> (read_table(adversary/<name>.csv), pd.read_csv(truth/adversary__<name>.csv, dtype=str) or None). load_identity_truth(root, domain, table) -> pd.read_csv(truth/<domain>__<table>.csv, dtype=str).fillna('') or None; scorecard uses identity.iloc[:,1] as person_id. load_holdout(root, domain, table) -> read_table(holdout/<domain>/<table>.csv) or None. _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:122-143; scorecard.py:139)_
- **io load_rowmap**: load_rowmap(path): read_csv(dtype=str); case-insensitive column lookup: protected_row column = first of ('protected_row','row','index','protected_index') present else the FIRST column; record id column = first of ('original_record_id','record_id','original_id') present else the LAST column. Output DataFrame columns exactly ['protected_row' (Int64, pd.to_numeric errors='coerce'), 'original_record_id' (str)] with NaN rows dropped. protected_row is the 0-based row index in the protected CSV (docstring). Several protected rows may map to the same original id and vice versa; nothing dedups here. _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:146-155; scorecard.py:8-9)_
- **io record_key**: record_key(catalog, domain, table, df): catalog rows with dataset==domain & table==table & privacy_role=='record_key' whose column exists in df -> that column; else first df column whose name ends with '_id' and df[c].is_unique; else None. Note scorecard calls it with the ORIGINAL frame (rk = io.record_key(cat, domain, table, orig)). _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:158-168; scorecard.py:73)_
- **io attack specs**: load_attack_specs(root) returns <root>/metadata/attack_specs.json['attacks'] ([] if root None or file absent). Each attack spec dict uses keys: dataset, table, adversary, qis, sensitive (optional), entity (optional), description (optional). The same file's top-level 'trajectories' list (keys dataset, table, user, time, lat, lon, place, p (default 4), temporal (default '1h'), spatial_m (default 500), description) is read directly in scorecard. _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:171-179; scorecard.py:115-128,143-160)_
- **scorecard run_scorecard signature**: run_scorecard(original_dir, protected_dir, scenario: Optional[str]=None, root=None, rowmaps: Optional[dict]=None, out_dir=None, max_adversary: int=3000) -> dict. domain = original_dir.name (folder name, e.g. 'health'). root = given or io.find_package_root(original_dir). Catalog loaded only if <root>/metadata/field_catalog.csv exists, else an empty frame with columns dataset,table,column,privacy_role,data_kind,subtype; then filtered to cat.dataset == domain. scenario dict loaded only if both scenario id and root are present. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:286-294)_
- **scorecard rowmap discovery**: rowmaps = dict(rowmaps or {}); every <protected_dir>/rowmap_*.csv is added with setdefault(stem minus 'rowmap_' prefix) (explicit --rowmap entries win); all are loaded with io.load_rowmap. A rowmap for table t is passed to evaluate_table as rms.get(t). Rowmaps therefore must be in the protected folder (or passed explicitly) and named rowmap_<table>.csv. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:297-300,309)_
- **scorecard table status**: For each ORIGINAL table t: if t not in protected tables -> report.tables[t] = {table, status:'withheld', rows_original}. Else evaluate_table(...) -> status 'released'; any exception -> {table, status:'error', error:'<Type>: <msg>', trace (traceback limit=3)}. Protected files with no original counterpart are listed in report['extra_protected_files'] and are NOT evaluated. Withheld tables contribute no risk components and no utility fallback other than whatever the utility task functions do with the missing table. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:304-315)_
- **scorecard JSON top-level**: scorecard.json keys: tool ('pets-eval 1.0.0'), dataset (domain), scenario (scenario dict, or the raw id string if not resolvable, or None), original (str path), protected (str path), tables ({table: per-table dict}), extra_protected_files (list), utility (list of task dicts), summary (composite() dict), risk_components ({'<table>: <risk name>': float}). Written with json.dumps(indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str) to <out_dir or protected_dir>/scorecard.json; HTML to scorecard.html; out_dir created with mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True). _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:301-323)_
- **scorecard per-table JSON**: evaluate_table(domain, table, orig, prot, cat, root, scenario, rowmap, max_adversary) -> dict with keys: table, status:'released', rows_original, rows_protected, columns_dropped (orig cols not in prot), columns_added (prot cols not in orig), direct_identifiers_retained ({col: share}), optional hash_attack ({col: result}), k_anonymity, optional k_anonymity_original, optional l_diversity, optional trajectory_unicity ({user_col: result}), row_alignment (str), optional linkage, optional free_text ({col: result}), optional synthetic ({dcr, optional membership_inference}), regex_residuals ({col: {kind: count}}), risks ({risk name: float rounded 4}), seconds. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:70-243)_
- **risk 1 direct identifiers**: For each catalog direct_identifier column present in BOTH orig and prot: values normalised (dropna, str, strip, lower, remove whitespace/-/.), share = mean of protected values present in the set of original values (0 if no values); recorded only if share > 0. Risk 'direct identifiers retained' = max share (0.0 if none). Dropping the column entirely yields 0 risk; a pseudonymised column whose values never equal any original value also yields 0. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:42-43,78-88)_
- **risk 2 hashed ids**: hcols = attacks.detect_hash_columns(prot); if any, candidates = unique original values of catalog direct_identifier + technical_identifier columns (capped at first 300000) and attacks.hash_dictionary_attack(prot[c], cands) per hashed column; result stored in r['hash_attack']; risk 'hashed ids reversible' = max of result['share_values_reversed'] (default 0.0). Detection heuristics are in attacks.py (not in scope). _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:90-98)_
- **risk 3 k-anonymity**: qis = catalog quasi_identifier columns kept in prot; sens = catalog sensitive_attribute columns kept in prot. If qis non-empty: r['k_anonymity'] = privacy.k_anonymity(prot, qis); r['k_anonymity_original'] = privacy.k_anonymity(orig, qis present in orig); risk 'records with k<5' = k_anonymity['share_below']['k<5']; if sens: r['l_diversity'] = privacy.l_diversity(prot, qis, sens[0]) (first sensitive col only). If no qis kept: k_anonymity = {'note': 'no catalogued quasi-identifier kept'} and no k risk. Keys used from k_anonymity result elsewhere: min_k, share_below (dict with 'k<5'). _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:100-111,369)_
- **risk 3b trajectory unicity**: If root: read metadata/attack_specs.json 'trajectories' entries matching dataset/table; kw = user_col, time_col, lat_col, lon_col, place_col, p, temporal, spatial_m, n_users=1000 (fixed sampling limit). If user column present in prot -> privacy.trajectory_unicity(prot, **kw) else {'evaluated': True, 'unicity': 0.0, 'note': '<user> removed: traces cannot be linked'}; baseline unicity on orig stored as unicity_original; 'attack' = description. Risk key `trajectory unicity (<user_col>)` = unicity when evaluated. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:113-128)_
- **row alignment / synthetic classification**: _record_ids_for_rows(prot, rowmap, rk, orig_ids): (1) rowmap given -> (rowmap, 'row map'); (2) else if rk (record key of ORIGINAL) is a column of prot and prot[rk].astype(str).isin(orig_ids).mean() > 0.5 -> synthetic rowmap {protected_row: arange(len(prot)), original_record_id: prot[rk]} with source 'original record ids kept in the release (itself a linkage key)'; (3) else (None, ''). r['row_alignment'] = source or 'none'. rm is None <=> table treated as synthetic/aggregate. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:58-67,132-133)_
- **synthetic branch consequences**: When rm is None: (a) if 'records with k<5' was computed it is REMOVED from risks and k_anonymity['note'] = 'not scored as a risk: rows are not linked to real records (synthetic or aggregate)'; (b) linkage = {'note': 'no row map: linkage not evaluated (treated as synthetic / aggregate release)'}; (c) each free-text column present in prot gets {'evaluated': False, 'reason': 'needs a row map to align texts'}; (d) section 6 synthetic runs if len(prot) > 0. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:134-137,185-186,202-204,215-230)_
- **risk 4 linkage preconditions**: Linkage runs only if rm is not None AND identity truth file truth/<domain>__<table>.csv exists AND its second column (iloc[:,1], person_id) has at least one non-empty value. temporal = catalog columns with data_kind=='temporal' for the table. orig_rm = {protected_row: arange(len(orig)), original_record_id: orig[rk]} if rk else None (used for the baseline on the original). _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:131-141)_
- **risk 4 attack plan**: specs = attack specs with dataset==domain & table==table. Branches: (i) no spec for this table but some spec exists for the domain -> plan = [] and linkage['note'] = 'no attack spec targets this table (metadata/attack_specs.json)' (no linkage risk component at all); (ii) specs exist -> adversaries = _adversaries_for(root, domain, scenario); chosen = specs whose 'adversary' is in that list, falling back to all specs; plan = [(adversary, spec)]; (iii) no specs for the domain at all -> plan = [(name, None) for every name from _adversaries_for]. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:143-153)_
- **adversary selection**: _adversaries_for(root, domain, scenario): names = adversary/*.csv stems that also have truth/adversary__<name>.csv; if scenario given, picked = names whose string appears inside json.dumps(scenario['threat_model']) (substring match); if non-empty return picked; else names containing domain.split('_')[0] as substring; else all names with truth. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:46-55)_
- **risk 4 per-adversary result**: For each (adv_name, sp): sens_col = sp['sensitive'] or first catalog sensitive_attribute, kept only if in orig.columns; q_p = attacks.qis_from_spec(sp['qis'], prot.columns), q_o likewise on orig.columns; ent = sp['entity']. If spec given and q_p empty -> res = {'evaluated': True, 'qis_used': [], 'reidentification_rate': 0.0, 'n_targets_in_data': None, 'note': 'every attacker column this attack needs was removed from the release'}. Else res = attacks.linkage_attack(adv, truth, prot, rm, identity, qis=q_p, original=orig, record_key=rk, sensitive=sens_col, temporal_cols=temporal, max_adversary=max_adversary, entity=ent). res['attack'] = description. If evaluated and orig_rm: baseline linkage_attack on orig (qis=q_o, no original/record_key/sensitive) -> res['baseline_reidentification_rate_original'], and if baseline rate truthy res['risk_reduction'] = round(1 - rate/baseline, 4). worst = max(worst, res['reidentification_rate'], res.get('attribute_inference',{}).get('advantage_over_base_rate', 0.0)). Any exception -> {'evaluated': False, 'reason': 'error: ...'}. r['linkage'][adv_name] = res. Risk 'linkage re-identification' = worst, added only if at least one adversary result has evaluated True. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:154-184)_
- **risk 5 free text**: tcols = catalog free_text columns present in orig. If tcols and root: per column: gold = load_spans(spans_path) if file exists else {}; no gold -> {'evaluated': False, 'reason': 'no gold spans in package'}; column absent from prot -> {'evaluated': True, 'status': 'withheld', 'identifying_leakage_rate': 0.0}; rm None -> {'evaluated': False, 'reason': 'needs a row map to align texts'}; else texts = {original_record_id: prot[c] at protected_row} for rowmap rows whose protected_row is within [0, len(prot)) (out-of-range rows silently dropped), res = text.redaction_leakage(gold, texts) with 'examples' key removed, stored as {'evaluated': True, **res}. Risk 'free-text identifier leakage' = max identifying_leakage_rate over evaluated columns (added only if any evaluated). Dropping a free-text column scores 0 leakage (not not_applicable). _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:188-213)_
- **risk 6 synthetic**: If rm is None and len(prot): excl = catalog direct_identifier + free_text + record_key + technical_identifier columns; cols = prot columns also in orig, not excluded, and with orig[c].nunique() < 0.5*len(orig). hold = load_holdout. If cols: r['synthetic']['dcr'] = privacy.dcr_report(prot, orig, hold, cols); if holdout present and non-empty: mia = privacy.membership_inference_auc(prot, orig, hold, cols) stored as synthetic['membership_inference'] and if mia['evaluated'] risk 'membership inference advantage' = mia['advantage']; if dcr['evaluated'] risk 'exact copies of original rows' = dcr['share_exact_copies']. If cols empty nothing is recorded under 'synthetic'. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:215-230)_
- **risk 7 regex residuals**: sample = prot.head(20000) (sampling limit); for every non-numeric, non-bool column, check.scan_text('\n'.join(non-null values as str)) -> counts dict; stored as r['regex_residuals'][col] = dict(counts) if non-empty. This is informational only: it is NOT added to risks. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:232-240)_
- **risks rounding**: r['risks'] = {name: round(float(v), 4)}; run_scorecard flattens to all_risks[f'{table}: {name}'] and this dict is both report['risk_components'] and the input to composite(). _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:241,313-318)_
- **utility task resolution**: run_utility(domain, orig_tables, prot_tables, scenario): tasks = [t for t in all_tasks([domain]) if t.dataset == domain]; required = set(scenario['utility_requirements']) (empty if no scenario); if scenario: sel = tasks whose id is in required OR whose t.scenarios list contains scenario['id']; tasks = sel or tasks (falls back to ALL domain tasks when nothing matches). Each task: res = t.fn(orig, prot) (both are {table: DataFrame} dicts); exception -> {'score': None, 'metric': 'error', 'detail': {'error': 'Type: msg', 'trace': ...}}. Output entry: {id, table, kind, description, required: (id in required) or (required set empty), **res}. So without a scenario every task is 'required'. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:246-261)_
- **utility task result shape**: Task fn results are merged via **res; keys consumed downstream: 'score' (float or None), 'metric' (str, optional), 'detail'. None score is rendered as 'n/a ' on stdout, blank in HTML table, and 'not answerable / not evaluated' in the HTML bar chart. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:255-260,336,374; cli.py:42)_
- **composite**: composite(risks, utility): vals = non-None risk values; privacy = 1 - (0.5*max(vals) + 0.5*mean(vals)) or None if no risks. us = [score or 0.0 for required tasks] + [score for optional tasks with score not None]; utility = mean(us) or None if empty. composite = (30+25)/(30/p + 25/u) with p,u floored at 1e-9, but forced to 0.0 if privacy<=0 or utility<=0; None if either is None. Returns {privacy, utility, composite (each rounded 4 or None), label: 'self-assessment, not the official judging score', method: 'privacy = 1 - (0.5*worst + 0.5*mean risk); utility = mean task score (required unanswerable = 0); composite = weighted harmonic mean (privacy 30, utility 25)'}. PRIV_W, UTIL_W = 30, 25. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:33,264-283)_
- **HTML**: render_html(report) produces a single self-contained page: title 'PETs scorecard — <dataset>'; scenario line (id — title, or raw string/'none'); three tiles Privacy (1 − risk) / Utility retained / Composite coloured green >=0.7, amber 0.4-0.7, red otherwise; SVG bar charts for risk_components (red, name truncated to 46 chars) and utility tasks (blue, '(optional)' suffix when not required, None -> 'not answerable / not evaluated'); Tables table with columns Table, Status, Rows (rows_protected), Direct ids retained, 'min k / share k<5', Linkage re-identification ('<adv>: xx% (original yy%)' per evaluated adversary), Regex residuals ('col:count'); Utility detail table (Task, Question, Score %.2f, Metric); footer note. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:327-391)_
- **sampling and limits**: Explicit limits in these files: --max-adversary default 3000 passed to attacks.linkage_attack (both protected and baseline runs); hash dictionary candidates capped at 300000; trajectory unicity n_users=1000; regex residual scan on prot.head(20000). No random seeds are set in scorecard.py, cli.py, io.py or __main__.py. _(toolkit/pets_eval/cli.py:118; scorecard.py:96,120,166-173,234)_
- **withheld semantics**: 'withheld' has two meanings: (1) a whole table absent from the protected folder -> tables[t].status == 'withheld' with only rows_original, no risks, no evaluation; (2) a free-text column absent from a released table -> free_text[col] = {'evaluated': True, 'status': 'withheld', 'identifying_leakage_rate': 0.0}. Docstring: withholding everything scores low on utility because required tasks that cannot be answered score 0. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:5-6,16,199-201,305-307)_
- **protected folder conventions**: Docstring conventions: same table file names as the original; keep original column names for kept columns (generalised values allowed, see pets_eval.parse); one rowmap per released microdata table named rowmap_<table>.csv with columns protected_row and original_record_id, used only for scoring and never published; no rowmap + no original record ids => treated as synthetic (DCR / membership inference). _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:5-10)_

Gotchas:
- Row alignment is auto-inferred even without a rowmap: if the protected table keeps the original record-key column and >50% of its values match original ids, the toolkit builds an identity rowmap (row i -> prot[rk][i]) and labels the source 'original record ids kept in the release (itself a linkage key)'. An adapter that pseudonymises record ids but does not ship a rowmap will therefore be scored as SYNTHETIC (no linkage, no free-text evaluation, k<5 not scored), which can look artificially safe. Ship rowmap_<table>.csv for every row-level table.
- rowmap_<table>.csv must sit in the protected folder (auto-discovery is protected_dir.glob('rowmap_*.csv')) or be passed via --rowmap table=path. io.load_tables skips rowmap_* and _* stems, so they do not get evaluated as extra tables, but any other extra file (e.g. a manifest.csv) is listed in extra_protected_files and ignored.
- load_rowmap column fallback: if neither recognised name is present it silently uses the FIRST column as protected_row and the LAST column as original_record_id. Use exactly 'protected_row' and 'original_record_id' headers to avoid surprises. protected_row is 0-based positional index into the protected CSV as pandas reads it (header excluded).
- The --rowmap CLI parsing uses str.replace('rowmap_', '') on the stem, not a prefix strip; and the scenario-based adversary selection is a substring search of the adversary file stem inside json.dumps(scenario['threat_model']).
- Dropping a catalogued free_text column scores leakage 0.0 and counts as evaluated (status 'withheld'); keeping it without a rowmap yields evaluated False (not a risk). There is no 'not_applicable' status in the toolkit: absent components are simply missing keys, so an adapter must derive not_applicable/unsupported itself from the presence of notes/'evaluated': False/'reason'.
- Utility: without a --scenario every task for the domain is treated as required (required = id in required or not required), and a task whose fn raises contributes score None -> counted as 0 in the utility mean. With a scenario whose utility_requirements/task scenarios match nothing, ALL domain tasks run (sel or tasks).
- If root cannot be found (no PETS_ROOT and no ancestor with metadata/ + data/|adversary/), the catalog is empty: no direct-identifier, QI, sensitive, free-text or linkage evaluation happens, risks are empty, privacy is None and composite is None. The adapter should pass --root explicitly.
- An exception inside evaluate_table marks the whole table status 'error' and drops all of its risk components; per-adversary and per-task exceptions are captured locally instead (evaluated False / score None).
- The table-status strings in the JSON are 'released' | 'withheld' | 'error' only; domain is derived from the ORIGINAL folder's basename (e.g. data/health -> 'health') and must match catalog.dataset, task.dataset, spans file prefixes and truth file prefixes.
- read_table forces str dtype on identifier-like column names (regex in io.py:24-25) but infers everything else; keep_default_na=True turns empty strings into NaN, which affects _norm_vals dropna and fillna('') in text alignment.
- k<5 share is computed on the protected table with catalog QIs that still exist under their original column names; renamed QI columns are invisible to k-anonymity, linkage qis_from_spec (behaviour in attacks.py) and the direct-identifier check alike.

Open questions:
- attacks.py (not in scope): exact signatures and result keys of detect_hash_columns, hash_dictionary_attack (share_values_reversed), qis_from_spec, linkage_attack (reidentification_rate, n_targets_in_data, qis_used, attribute_inference.advantage_over_base_rate, how max_adversary samples rows, whether a random seed is used, how 'entity' and temporal_cols change matching).
- privacy.py (not in scope): result schemas and sampling/seeds of k_anonymity (min_k, share_below keys), l_diversity, trajectory_unicity (n_users sampling), dcr_report (evaluated, share_exact_copies), membership_inference_auc (evaluated, advantage).
- text.py (not in scope): schema of redaction_leakage (identifying_leakage_rate, examples, other keys) and span_scores; what counts as 'identifying' labels.
- check.py (not in scope): scan_text/scan_path regex kinds, the 'note' text, --max-lines semantics.
- utility package (not in scope): all_tasks(datasets) registry, Task fields (id, dataset, table, kind, description, scenarios, fn), per-task metric names and how a missing (withheld) table or missing columns are reported (score None vs 0), whether tasks use random sampling/seeds.
- detect.py (not in scope): expected columns of the --pred CSV and the score_detection result schema (errors, confusion keys).
- parse.py (not in scope): which generalised value formats (ranges, prefixes, bins) are accepted for QIs and dates.
- Actual contents/existence of metadata/scenarios.json (field names beyond id, dataset, trust_level, title, threat_model, utility_requirements), metadata/attack_specs.json (attacks and trajectories entries per dataset), truth/, holdout/ and adversary/ folders in this package were not inspected.
- Whether rowmaps may be many-to-one (several protected rows for one original record) or one-to-many, and how attacks.linkage_attack and text alignment treat duplicates (scorecard's dict(zip(...)) keeps the last protected row per original_record_id for free text).
- field_catalog.csv full column list (beyond dataset, table, column, privacy_role, data_kind, subtype, art9_special_category) and the full set of privacy_role values.
- Python environment: pyproject only declares dependencies; whether the toolkit is installed (pip install -e toolkit) or run via PYTHONPATH/python -m pets_eval was not verified.

## Reader: text_utility

All five toolkit files were read completely. text.py provides two scoring paths over in-memory dicts keyed by record_id: span_scores(gold, pred) (greedy one-to-one match, per-label P/R/F1/F2) and redaction_leakage(gold, protected_texts) (normalised substring survival with PHONE variants, min normalised length 3, records absent from protected_texts skipped entirely). check.py is a regex+validator scanner (scan_text / scan_path) over .csv/.json/.jsonl/.txt/.md/.tsv files, returning {files, totals, examples(masked), n_files_scanned, note}, with PAYMENT_CARD-specific branches (date/GSRN skip, IMEI relabel). parse.py defines the tolerant parsers (parse_numeric with _RANGE/_PLUS/_LT regexes, to_datetime with ISO/Finnish/week/month/year fallbacks, postcode_prefix, age bands, tvd, table_mape, score_from_rel_error). utility/__init__.py defines UtilityTask(id, dataset, table, description, kind, fn(orig, prot), needs, scenarios), result() clamping score to [0,1] or None, not_answerable(missing) and require(df, cols) which treats a None table as all columns missing. customer_service.py defines CS-U1..U7 over tables "turns" and "conversations", each returning not_answerable when required columns are absent and otherwise degrading numerically; it also has its own span_scores (no one-to-one matching, f-key "f2"), leak_rate (case-insensitive verbatim, min_len 4, no separator normalisation) and load_spans (JSONL lines with record_id + spans). None of these files contains a CLI, a staging-folder layout, rowmap handling, attacks, or the evaluated/not_applicable/unsupported/failed status taxonomy; those are listed as open questions.

- **text: span input shape**: Spans = dict of {record_id: [ {start, end, label, text?}, ... ]}; both gold and pred use this shape, keyed by record_id. _(toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:17)_
- **text: IDENTIFYING labels**: IDENTIFYING = {PERSON, NATIONAL_ID, EMAIL, PHONE, ADDRESS, IBAN, PAYMENT_CARD, ACCOUNT_NUMBER, IP_ADDRESS, LICENSE_PLATE, USERNAME, SECRET, DEVICE_ID, PROPERTY_ID, URL}; LOCATION/DATE/ORG/HEALTH are not in it and are excluded from identifying_leakage_rate. _(toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:19-21)_
- **text: _prf**: _prf(tp, fp, fn) returns {precision, recall, f1, f2, tp, fp, fn}; f2 = 5*p*r/(4*p+r); all rates rounded to 4 decimals, counts cast to int; 0.0 when a denominator is 0. _(toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:24-30)_
- **text: span_scores signature**: def span_scores(gold: Spans, pred: Spans, mode: str = "overlap", label_agnostic: bool = False, labels: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None) -> dict. mode 'exact' requires same start and end; 'overlap' requires a['start'] < b['end'] and b['start'] < a['end']. Records missing from pred count as predicting nothing; records only in pred add false positives. _(toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:33-40)_
- **text: span_scores matching**: Matching is greedy one-to-one: each gold span takes the first unused pred span that matches (same label unless label_agnostic). Unmatched gold -> fn under gold label. Unmatched pred -> fp under pred label ("?" if pred has no label, "ANY" if label_agnostic), except in overlap mode a pred that overlaps any gold span of the record is not counted as fp (no double penalty). labels filter applies to gold always and to pred unless label_agnostic. _(toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:41-67)_
- **text: span_scores output**: Returns {"mode": mode, "per_label": {label: _prf dict}, "micro": _prf dict over summed tp/fp/fn, "flat": {label: {gold: tp+fn, recall, precision, f2}, "_micro": {...}}, "n_records": len(set(gold)|set(pred))}. per_label keys sorted. 'flat' deliberately mirrors customer_service.span_scores layout. _(toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:68-74)_
- **text: normalise**: _SEP = re.compile(r"[\s\-\.\(\)/_:]+"); normalise(s) = _SEP.sub("", str(s).lower()) -> lower-case and remove whitespace, hyphen, dot, parentheses, slash, underscore, colon. _(toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:77-82)_
- **text: _variants**: _variants(value, label): set starts with normalise(value); for label == "PHONE" also adds digits-only form (re.sub(r"\D","")), and if digits start with "358" adds "0"+digits[3:], elif start with "0" adds "358"+digits[1:]. Variants shorter than 2 chars are dropped. _(toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:85-95)_
- **text: redaction_leakage signature and inputs**: def redaction_leakage(gold: Spans, protected_texts: dict, labels: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None, original_texts: Optional[dict] = None) -> dict. protected_texts is {record_id: protected text}. Span value = s["text"], else original_texts[rid][start:end] if original_texts given; spans with no value are skipped. _(toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:98-120)_
- **text: redaction_leakage record handling**: A record_id in gold but not in protected_texts is skipped with `continue` (treated as withheld: it contributes nothing to n or leaked). A present record with None/empty text normalises to "" (nothing leaks but spans still count in n). _(toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:109-112)_
- **text: redaction_leakage min length and case**: Spans whose normalised value has length < 3 are skipped (1-2 char values such as initials are not testable). Leak test: any(v in pt for v in _variants(val, label)) where pt = normalise(protected text) -> case-insensitive, separator-insensitive substring match. _(toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:121-124)_
- **text: redaction_leakage output**: Returns {"leakage_rate": leaked/n, "leakage_rate_chars": leaked_chars/chars, "identifying_leakage_rate": leaked/n over labels in IDENTIFYING, "per_label": {label: {n, leaked, rate}} sorted by label, "n_values": total n, "examples": up to 20 of {record_id, label, value}}. Rates rounded to 4 decimals, 0.0 when denominator is 0. chars counted as len(val) of the raw (un-normalised) value. The examples contain the raw leaked PII value, unmasked. _(toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:125-146)_
- **text: spans_from_redaction**: def spans_from_redaction(original: str, protected: str) -> list[dict]: uses difflib.SequenceMatcher(autojunk=False); every 'replace' or 'delete' opcode with i2 > i1 becomes {start: i1, end: i2, label: "ANY"} in original-text offsets. _(toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:149-158)_
- **check: patterns**: PATTERNS (group 1 is the value): NATIONAL_ID r"(?<![0-9A-Za-z])(\d{6}[-+ABCDEFUVWXY]\d{3}[0-9A-Y])(?![0-9A-Za-z])"; IBAN r"(?<![A-Z0-9])([A-Z]{2}\d{2}(?: ?[A-Z0-9]{4}){2,7}(?: ?[A-Z0-9]{1,4})?)(?![A-Z0-9])" (case-sensitive); PAYMENT_CARD r"(?<![0-9A-Za-z])((?:\d[ -]?){12,18}\d)(?![0-9A-Za-z])"; EMAIL r"(?<![\w.+-])([\w.+-]+@[\w-]+(?:\.[\w-]+)+)" re.I; PHONE r"(?<![\d+])((?:\+358|00358|\b0)[ -]?(?:4\d|50)[ -]?\d{3,4}[ -]?\d{3,4})(?!\d)"; IP_ADDRESS r"(?<![\d.])((?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3})(?![\d.])"; IPV6 r"(?<![0-9a-f:])((?:[0-9a-f]{1,4}:){4,7}[0-9a-f]{1,4})(?![0-9a-f:])" re.I; MAC_ADDRESS r"(?<![0-9A-F:-])((?:[0-9A-F]{2}[:-]){5}[0-9A-F]{2})(?![0-9A-F:-])" re.I; LICENSE_PLATE r"(?<![A-ZÅÄÖ0-9-])([A-ZÅÄÖ]{2,3}-\d{1,3})(?![0-9-])". _(toolkit/pets_eval/check.py:17-27)_
- **check: validators**: VALIDATORS = {NATIONAL_ID: hetu_ok, IBAN: iban_ok, PAYMENT_CARD: luhn_ok, IP_ADDRESS: ip_ok, IPV6: ip_ok}. hetu_ok: HETU_CHECK[int(s[:6]+s[7:10]) % 31] == s[10] with HETU_CHECK="0123456789ABCDEFHJKLMNPRSTUVWXY". iban_ok: spaces removed, 15<=len<=34, base-36 rearranged int % 97 == 1. luhn_ok: digits only, 13..19 digits, not all identical, must match _IIN prefix regex r"^(4\d|5[1-5]|2(2[2-9]|[3-6]\d|7[01]|720)|3[47]|6011|65|64[4-9]|35(2[89]|[3-8]\d)|62)", then Luhn sum % 10 == 0. ip_ok: ipaddress.ip_address parses. PHONE, LICENSE_PLATE, EMAIL, MAC_ADDRESS have no validator (pattern-only). _(toolkit/pets_eval/check.py:15,30-75)_
- **check: mask**: mask(v) returns v[:2] + "…" + v[-2:] if len(v) > 5 else "…"; used for report examples only. _(toolkit/pets_eval/check.py:78-80)_
- **check: scan_text branches**: def scan_text(text: str, counts: Optional[dict] = None, examples: Optional[dict] = None) -> dict. For each pattern match: skip if a validator exists and fails. PAYMENT_CARD extra branches: skip if re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}.*", v) (date) or (18 digits and starts with "643") (metering-point GSRN); relabel to "IMEI" if 15 digits and first two digits in ("35","86","01"). Otherwise counts[label] += 1 and up to 3 masked examples per label are stored in examples[label]. _(toolkit/pets_eval/check.py:83-102)_
- **check: scan_path signature and output**: def scan_path(path, max_lines: Optional[int] = None, exts=(".csv", ".json", ".jsonl", ".txt", ".md", ".tsv")) -> dict. A file is scanned alone; a folder is rglob'd recursively (sorted) for files whose lower-cased suffix is in exts. Files read with encoding utf-8, errors=replace, line by line; max_lines caps lines per file. Output: {"files": {str(path): {label: count}} (only files with at least one hit), "totals": {label: count}, "examples": {label: [masked, ...]}, "n_files_scanned": int, "note": str}. _(toolkit/pets_eval/check.py:105-126)_
- **check: note text**: report["note"] = "Synthetic identifiers in this package use reserved formats; any hit means a value survived your transformation. PHONE and LICENSE_PLATE are pattern-only (possible false positives)." _(toolkit/pets_eval/check.py:124-125)_
- **parse: documented generalised forms**: Docstring lists accepted forms: ages 37 | "37" | "30-39" | "30–39" | "[30,40)" | "30+" | "90+"; dates ISO date/time, rounded times, "2025-03" (month), "2025-W12" (ISO week), "2025" (year); postcodes "20100" | "201**" | "201" | "20100-20199"; coordinates floats of any precision or grid ids from latlon_to_grid; numbers 12.5 | "12,5" | "10-20" (range -> midpoint) | "<5" (-> 2.5) | "" -> NaN. _(toolkit/pets_eval/parse.py:1-9)_
- **parse: regexes**: _RANGE = r"^\s*[\[(]?\s*(-?\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)\s*(?:-|–|,|\.\.)\s*(-?\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)\s*[\])]?\s*$"; _PLUS = r"^\s*(\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)\s*\+\s*$"; _LT = r"^\s*<\s*(\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)\s*$". _(toolkit/pets_eval/parse.py:17-19)_
- **parse: parse_numeric**: def parse_numeric(s: pd.Series, open_upper_width: float = 10.0) -> pd.Series. Numeric dtype -> astype(float). Per value: None/NaN -> NaN; stripped text "" or lower in ("nan","none","null","*","suppressed") -> NaN; try float(t.replace(",",".").replace(" ","")); else _RANGE -> (lo+hi)/2 with hi -= 1e-9 when the text starts with "[" and ends with ")"; else _PLUS -> N + open_upper_width/2 ("90+" -> 95); else _LT -> N/2 ("<5" -> 2.5); else NaN. _(toolkit/pets_eval/parse.py:22-51)_
