- **parse: to_age_band / age_from_birth**: to_age_band(s, width=10, top=80): parse_numeric then floor to band start clipped at top; labels "0-9"... "70-79", "80+"; NaN stays NaN. age_from_birth(s, ref="2025-12-31") = (ref - to_date(s)).days / 365.25. _(toolkit/pets_eval/parse.py:54-64)_
- **parse: to_datetime**: def to_datetime(s: pd.Series) -> pd.Series. Datetime dtype returned as-is. Fast path pd.to_datetime(errors="coerce", format="ISO8601"). If that introduced new NaNs, remaining values get Finnish day-first rewrite r"^(\d{1,2})\.(\d{1,2})\.(\d{4})(?:\s+(?:klo\s+)?(\d{1,2})[.:](\d{2}))?" -> "YYYY-MM-DD[ HH:MM]" then pd.to_datetime(format="mixed"). Still-bad non-empty values go through one(): ISO week r"^(\d{4})-?W(\d{1,2})$" -> Monday of that week (fromisocalendar), r"^\d{4}$" -> YYYY-01-01, r"^\d{4}-\d{2}$" -> YYYY-MM-01, else pd.Timestamp(t) else NaT. _(toolkit/pets_eval/parse.py:67-106)_
- **parse: date helpers**: to_date = to_datetime(...).dt.normalize(); to_week -> "YYYY-Www" (ISO year/week, zero-padded) or NaN; to_month -> "%Y-%m"; to_hour -> .dt.hour. _(toolkit/pets_eval/parse.py:109-125)_
- **parse: postcode_prefix**: def postcode_prefix(s: pd.Series, n: int = 3): strip, remove all non-digits (regex [^0-9]), take first n chars, keep only where length == n. So "201**" -> "201", "20100-20199" -> "201" (digits "2010020199"[:3]), "201" -> "201"; values with fewer than n digits become NaN. _(toolkit/pets_eval/parse.py:128-130)_
- **parse: latlon_to_grid**: latlon_to_grid(lat, lon, cell_m=1000): parse_numeric both; y = floor(lat*111320/cell_m), x = floor(lon*111320*cos(radians(60.45))/cell_m); id = f"{y}_{x}" (Int64 strings); NaN where either coordinate is NaN. _(toolkit/pets_eval/parse.py:133-139)_
- **parse: scoring helpers**: rel_error(a,b) = |a-b|/max(|a|,1e-9), 0 if both 0. score_from_rel_error(err, tolerance=0.5) = max(0, 1 - err/tolerance), 0.0 if err is None/NaN. tvd(p,q): union index, fill 0, returns 1.0 if either sums to 0, else 0.5*sum|p/Σp - q/Σq|. table_mape(orig, prot, min_count=0): union index, missing cells = 0, mean of |o-p|/o over cells with o > min_count, NaN if no such cells. _(toolkit/pets_eval/parse.py:142-173)_
- **utility: contract**: A utility task answers one question on ORIGINAL and PROTECTED tables; score 1.0 = identical, 0.0 = useless, None = not answerable because required columns were removed or coarsened beyond what the task needs. orig / prot are dicts {table_name: DataFrame}; protected tables keep original column names for the columns they keep, values may be generalised per pets_eval.parse. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/__init__.py:1-10)_
- **utility: DOMAINS**: DOMAINS = ["health", "mobility", "smart_city", "energy", "finance", "cyber", "education", "public_admin", "customer_service"]. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/__init__.py:17-18)_
- **utility: UtilityTask dataclass**: @dataclass UtilityTask: id: str; dataset: str; table: str; description: str; kind: str (aggregate | distribution | relationship | model | detection | text); fn: Callable[[dict, dict], dict] called as fn(orig, prot); needs: list (columns used, informational only, not enforced); scenarios: list. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/__init__.py:21-30)_
- **utility: result / not_answerable / require**: result(score, metric, **detail): if score is not None it is clamped float(max(0.0, min(1.0, score))); returns {"score": score, "metric": metric, "detail": detail}. not_answerable(missing) = result(None, "not answerable", missing=list(missing)). require(df, cols) returns [c for c in cols if df is None or c not in df.columns] -> a missing table makes every column missing. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/__init__.py:33-44)_
- **utility: all_tasks**: all_tasks(domains=None) imports pets_eval.utility.{domain} for each domain (default DOMAINS), skips ModuleNotFoundError, concatenates each module's TASKS list. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/__init__.py:47-55)_
- **customer_service: span_scores (second implementation)**: def span_scores(gold, pred, labels=None, mode="overlap", typed=False, beta=2.0) -> dict. Not one-to-one: a gold span is recall-hit if any pred span overlaps (positive overlap length) / exactly matches it (and same label if typed); a pred span is precision-hit if it overlaps any gold span. labels default to sorted labels in gold. Output {label: {gold, recall, precision, "f2"}, "_micro": {gold, recall, precision, "f2"}}; recall/precision are NaN when a label has no gold/pred (treated as 0 in F); F key is f"f{beta:g}". Pred without label is bucketed "ANY". _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:18-59)_
- **customer_service: leak_rate**: def leak_rate(gold: dict, original_text: dict, protected_text: dict, min_len: int = 4) -> dict. pt = str(protected_text.get(rid, "") or "").lower() (missing records count as empty text, i.e. counted in totals as not leaked, unlike text.redaction_leakage which skips them). Value = s["text"] or original_text.get(rid,"")[start:end]; skipped if len(v.strip()) < 4. Leak = v.lower() in pt (verbatim, case-insensitive, no separator normalisation, no PHONE variants). Returns {label: leaked/total, "_overall": Σleaked/max(1,Σtotal)}. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:62-76)_
- **customer_service: load_spans**: load_spans(path): reads JSONL, one JSON object per line with keys "record_id" and "spans"; returns {record_id: spans}. This is the only file-format reader for spans in the five files. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:79-86)_
- **customer_service: _docs**: _docs(turns, convs, ids): filters turns by conversation_id in ids; sorts by ["conversation_id","seq"] only if a "seq" column exists; groups by conversation_id and joins text (NaN -> "") with " \n ". Returns Series indexed by conversation_id. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:90-92)_
- **customer_service: _intent_f1**: TfidfVectorizer(sublinear_tf=True, min_df=2, ngram_range=(1,2), max_features=60000) + LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, C=4.0); returns sklearn macro F1 on test docs. Requires scikit-learn at runtime. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:95-103)_
- **CS-U1 intent classifier**: u1_intent(orig, prot): tables orig["turns"], orig["conversations"], prot["turns"], prot["conversations"]. Required protected columns: turns[conversation_id, text], conversations[conversation_id, intent] else not_answerable. Original conversations must have split with values "train"/"eval" (used unguarded). Original F1 cached by key ("u1", id(ot), len(ot)). Protected train ids: if prot conversations has a "split" column use pc.split == "train", else map pc.conversation_id through original split (ids that do not map are dropped). If fewer than 50 protected train docs -> not_answerable(["train conversations"]). Protected labels come from protected conversations.intent reindexed on protected doc ids. Score = f_protected / f_original (None if f_original == 0), metric "macro-F1 ratio (protected-trained / original-trained) on original eval", detail f1_original, f1_protected (rounded 4). _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:106-129)_
- **CS-U1 degradation**: Tokenised/pseudonymised conversation_id that is not in the original split map and no protected split column -> conversation excluded from training; <50 remaining -> not answerable. Generalised intent values become the training labels so predictions on original eval labels fail -> F1 drops. Suppressed/empty text -> empty docs, lower F1. Score clamped to [0,1] by result(). _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:122-129; utility/__init__.py:33-36)_
- **CS-U2 sentiment vs CSAT**: u2_sent_csat: table conversations; requires protected [sentiment, csat]. sentiment mapped via _SENT = {"negative":0, "neutral":1, "positive":2} (any other value -> NaN); csat via pd.to_numeric(errors="coerce") (NOT parse_numeric, so ranges like "3-4" -> NaN). Spearman rho computed only if > 10 valid pairs else NaN. If protected rho is NaN -> score 0.0 with metric "Spearman(sentiment, csat) difference"; else score 1 - |rho_o - rho_p| / 0.5, metric "1 - |Δ Spearman(sentiment, CSAT)| / 0.5", detail rho_original, rho_protected. Requires scipy. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:132-152)_
- **CS-U3 intent mix**: u3_intent_mix: table conversations; requires protected [intent]. score = 1 - 2*tvd(orig intent value_counts, prot intent value_counts), metric "1 - 2·TVD of intent distribution", detail tvd. Generalised/renamed intent labels count as different categories, raising TVD; suppressed rows change counts. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:155-161)_
- **CS-U4 average handle time**: u4_aht: table conversations; requires protected [intent, handle_time_s]. Protected handle_time_s parsed with parse_numeric (ranges, "N+", "<N" accepted; "*"/"suppressed"/"" -> NaN and ignored by mean). Original uses raw .mean(). Compares group means by intent with table_mape (missing protected intent cells count as 0 -> 100% error for that cell), score = score_from_rel_error(mape, 0.5), metric "mean handle time by intent, MAPE (0.5 → score 0)", detail mape. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:164-173)_
- **CS-U5 vocabulary retention**: u5_vocab: table turns; requires protected [turn_id, text]. Token regex _TOK = r"[a-zåäöéü]{3,}" on lower-cased text. Common vocabulary = tokens appearing in >= 25 distinct original conversations (cached by ("u5", id(ot), len(ot))). Samples min(20000, len(orig turns)) original turns with random_state=7. Protected text looked up by turn_id via pt.set_index("turn_id").text; a turn_id absent from protected -> "" (all tokens lost). kept = Σ min(orig count, prot count) per common token; score = kept/total, metric "share of common (non-identifying) word tokens retained, matched by turn_id", detail retained. Turns with no common tokens are skipped. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:176-204)_
- **CS-U5 degradation**: Tokenised/renumbered turn_id breaks the join -> score ~0 even if text is intact. Replacing ordinary words with placeholder tokens that do not match the original word reduces kept. Surrogates for names do not hurt unless the name was in the >=25-conversation common set. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:193-202)_
- **CS-U6 channel x language**: u6_channel_lang: table conversations; requires protected [channel, language]. Compares groupby(["channel","language"]).size() via table_mape (missing or relabelled cells -> 0), score = score_from_rel_error(mape, 0.5), metric "contacts by channel × language, MAPE", detail mape. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:207-215)_
- **CS-U7 first-contact resolution**: u7_resolution: table conversations; requires protected [intent, resolved]. resolved is truthy iff str(value).lower() in ["true","1","yes"] (anything else, including suppressed, counts False). Resolution rate per intent; index = original intents; protected intents missing from that index get abs diff 1 (fillna(1)); err = mean abs diff; score = 1 - err/0.2, metric "first-contact resolution rate by intent, mean abs. difference (0.2 → score 0)", detail mae. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:218-228)_
- **customer_service: TASKS registry**: TASKS: CS-U1 (table turns, kind model, needs [turns.text, conversations.intent], scenarios [CS-S1, CS-S2]); CS-U2 (conversations, relationship, [sentiment, csat], [CS-S2]); CS-U3 (conversations, distribution, [intent], [CS-S1]); CS-U4 (conversations, aggregate, [intent, handle_time_s], [CS-S1, CS-S3]); CS-U5 (turns, text, [turns.text], [CS-S1, CS-S2]); CS-U6 (conversations, aggregate, [channel, language], [CS-S3]); CS-U7 (conversations, aggregate, [intent, resolved], [CS-S3]). dataset = "customer_service". _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:13,231-242)_
- **customer_service: table/column names used**: Table keys used: "turns" and "conversations". Columns referenced: turns[conversation_id, seq (optional), turn_id, text]; conversations[conversation_id, split (orig required; prot optional), intent, sentiment, csat, handle_time_s, channel, language, resolved]. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:91,107-127,137,157,166,181,193,209,220)_

Gotchas:
- There are two different span scorers and two different leakage scorers: text.span_scores/redaction_leakage (text.py:37,98) vs customer_service.span_scores/leak_rate (customer_service.py:22,62). They disagree on one-to-one matching, on records missing from protected text (text.py skips them; customer_service counts them as empty text), on min length (normalised < 3 vs raw stripped < 4) and on normalisation (text.py strips separators and adds PHONE +358/0 variants; customer_service is verbatim lower-case). An adapter must state which one it reports.
- text.redaction_leakage 'examples' holds the raw leaked PII value (text.py:132), not masked; check.py examples are masked (check.py:78-80,100). Do not copy text leakage examples into shared reports.
- text.redaction_leakage silently drops gold records absent from protected_texts (text.py:110-111); if the adapter withholds or renames record_ids, leakage_rate can look perfect while n_values shrinks. Report n_values alongside the rate.
- require() returns all columns as missing when the table itself is None (utility/__init__.py:43-44), so a missing protected table yields not_answerable with every column listed, not a distinct 'table missing' status.
- The 'needs' field on UtilityTask is informational only (utility/__init__.py:29); actual requirements are what each fn passes to require(), e.g. CS-U1 also needs conversation_id in both protected tables and 'split' in the original conversations (customer_service.py:109-113).
- CS-U1 and CS-U5 join protected to original by conversation_id / turn_id (customer_service.py:122,193); pseudonymising those keys without a protected 'split' column (U1) or at all (U5) silently degrades the score instead of returning not answerable.
- CS-U2 uses pd.to_numeric on csat, not parse_numeric (customer_service.py:145), so a generalised range like '3-4' becomes NaN; with <=10 valid pairs rho is NaN and the score is hard 0.0, not None (customer_service.py:147-151).
- CS-U7 treats any resolved value outside {'true','1','yes'} (case-insensitive) as False (customer_service.py:223); suppressing to '*' or 'suppressed' is scored as unresolved, not as missing.
- parse_numeric does not understand postcode masks like '201**' (parse.py:22-51 returns NaN); only postcode_prefix (parse.py:128-130) handles them, and it keeps a prefix only when exactly n digits remain.
- table_mape counts a cell present in the original but absent in the protected aggregate as 100% error (parse.py:165-173), so renaming/generalising a grouping key (intent, channel, language) is penalised as heavily as dropping rows.
- check.py IBAN regex is case-sensitive uppercase and NATIONAL_ID requires an uppercase century/check char; lower-casing a surviving identifier would evade the scanner but not text.redaction_leakage. PHONE regex only matches Finnish mobile forms (+358/00358/0 followed by 4x or 50).
- check.scan_path scans every line of every matching file under the folder recursively, including any JSON/JSONL rowmaps or reports placed inside the scanned path (check.py:105-116); keep rowmaps and reports outside the folder passed to the residual check, or they will be counted as leaks.
- Running these modules needs numpy, pandas, scikit-learn (CS-U1), and scipy (CS-U2); the Node adapter must shell out to a Python environment that has them.
- ISO-week parsing maps '2025-W12' to the Monday of that week and '2025-03' to the 1st of the month (parse.py:67-88); generalising timestamps to those forms shifts every value to the period start, which affects any task comparing means or hours (not used by CS-U1..U7, but relevant for other domains).

Open questions:
- No CLI commands or flags exist in the five files; the runner that wires check/text/utility together, its argument names, and how it emits per-test status (evaluated / not_applicable / unsupported / failed) are elsewhere in the toolkit and were not read.
- The staging-folder layout the toolkit accepts (file names for protected tables, rowmaps, gold jsonl, predicted spans jsonl, protected text CSV and which CSV column holds the protected text) is not defined in these files; only load_spans (customer_service.py:79-86) shows the JSONL span format {record_id, spans}. The loader that builds protected_texts / orig / prot dicts from disk is unknown.
- The attack modules (re-identification, linkage, etc.) and their inputs/outputs are not in the read set.
- Which span/leakage scorer the official evaluation uses for customer_service (text.py's or customer_service.py's) is not stated in these files.
- Scenario ids CS-S1, CS-S2, CS-S3 are referenced (customer_service.py:233-241) but their definitions (which tasks/attacks are required, thresholds) are not in the read files.
- The customer_service dataset schema (actual CSV file names, full column lists, split values, csat scale, resolved encoding) is inferred only from how the tasks use columns; the dataset's own schema/README was not read.
- How 'sampling limits' are expressed (max_lines for check.scan_path is the only one visible; CS-U5 samples 20000 turns with random_state=7) and whether other tasks or attacks have limits is unknown.
- Whether the runner passes original_texts to redaction_leakage (so gold spans without 'text' can be sliced) or requires 'text' in gold jsonl is not determined by these files.

## Reader: baselines

The TrustED pets-eval toolkit (/Users/markp/Code/sinceai-trusted/TRUSTED_SinceAI2026_FINAL/TRUSTED_PETS_PROVING_GROUND_2026/toolkit/pets_eval) scores a "protected folder" against the original dataset folder via a single Python entry point, pets_eval.scorecard.run_scorecard(original_dir, protected_dir, scenario=None, root=None, rowmaps=None, out_dir=None, max_adversary=3000) -> dict (CLI: `pets-eval scorecard --original data/customer_service --protected <staging> [--scenario CS-S1] [--rowmap rowmap_x.csv|table=path] [--root R] [--out DIR] [--max-adversary 3000]`). A staging folder is: one CSV per released table with the SAME file name as the original (customers.csv, conversations.csv, turns.csv), original column names kept for kept columns, plus rowmap_<table>.csv with columns protected_row (0-based row index into the protected CSV) and original_record_id (the catalog record_key value of the original row: customer_id / conversation_id / turn_id). The baselines build the rowmap trivially because they preserve row order: protected_row=range(len(df)), original_record_id=orig[record_key].astype(str). Presence of a rowmap (or raw record_key ids still in the release) is what makes a table "row-level": row_alignment="row map", k<5 share is scored, linkage attacks run, free-text leakage is scored. No rowmap and no original ids => table treated as synthetic (k reported not scored, linkage skipped, free-text "needs a row map", DCR/membership-inference instead). Baselines redact text with pure regex substitution into "[LABEL]" tokens (NATIONAL_ID, EMAIL, IBAN, URL, PAYMENT_CARD, PHONE, IP_ADDRESS, MAC, LICENSE_PLATE) and do NOT emit spans; the scorecard needs no spans, it tests whether each gold span's text (normalised: lowercase, separators stripped, phone 358/0 variants) still occurs in the protected text keyed by original_record_id. Per-table status values in the report are "released" / "withheld" / "error"; per-task utility is {score: float|null, metric, detail} where null metric "not answerable" carries detail.missing. The shipped results/ folder holds only scorecard.json/html per baseline (no protected CSVs or rowmaps are shipped), so the adapter must regenerate staging folders. Reference numbers for customer_service: B0 privacy 0.2222 / utility 1.0 / composite 0.3438; B2 0.3126 / 0.8557 / 0.4394; B2K 0.4952 / 0.8557 / 0.6125. Note B2/B2K lose CS-U1 ("not answerable: train conversations") because they HMAC-tokenise turns.conversation_id (technical_identifier) but leave conversations.conversation_id (record_key) raw, breaking the turns→conversations join.

- **Package root and layout**: Package root contains data/<domain>/<table>.csv, metadata/field_catalog.csv, metadata/scenarios.json, metadata/attack_specs.json, metadata/pii_spans/<domain>__<table>__<column>.jsonl, adversary/<name>.csv, truth/adversary__<name>.csv (adv_row_id->person_id), truth/<domain>__<table>.csv (record_id->person_id), holdout/<domain>/<table>.csv, toolkit/pets_eval (python package pets-eval 1.0.0, deps numpy>=1.24 pandas>=2.0 scipy>=1.10 scikit-learn>=1.2, python>=3.10), baselines/, examples/quickstart.py, results/. _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:3-11; toolkit/pyproject.toml; ls of package root)_
- **Install / invoke**: `pip install -e ./toolkit` or `export PYTHONPATH=$PWD/toolkit`; console script `pets-eval` -> pets_eval.cli:main. Package root auto-detected by walking up from original_dir (or $PETS_ROOT) to a folder with metadata/ and data/ or adversary/. _(toolkit/README.md:7-14; toolkit/pyproject.toml [project.scripts]; toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:28-39)_
- **CLI scorecard command**: `pets-eval scorecard --original <dir> --protected <dir> [--rowmap PATH|table=PATH (repeatable)] [--scenario ID] [--root DIR] [--out DIR] [--max-adversary N(default 3000)]`. --rowmap without '=' derives table name as Path(r).stem.replace('rowmap_',''). Prints summary lines 'privacy X utility Y composite Z', one 'risk' line per risk component, one 'util' line per task, then 'wrote <out>/scorecard.json and <out>/scorecard.html'. _(toolkit/pets_eval/cli.py:26-44, 111-119)_
- **Other CLI commands**: `pets-eval detect --pred CSV [--catalog] [--root] [--datasets a,b] [--out]` (pred CSV must have columns dataset,table,column and optionally privacy_role,subtype); `pets-eval text --gold metadata/pii_spans/<d>__<t>__<c>.jsonl (--pred spans.jsonl | --protected file.csv --text-col COL (--id-col ID | --rowmap R)) [--out]`; `pets-eval check PATH [--max-lines N] [--out]`; `pets-eval tasks [--dataset D]`; `pets-eval scenarios [--dataset D] [--root]`. _(toolkit/pets_eval/cli.py:47-147; toolkit/pets_eval/detect.py:23-33)_
- **run_scorecard signature**: def run_scorecard(original_dir, protected_dir, scenario: Optional[str] = None, root=None, rowmaps: Optional[dict] = None, out_dir=None, max_adversary: int = 3000) -> dict. domain = original_dir.name; catalog filtered to that dataset; tables loaded from both dirs with io.load_tables (every *.csv/*.parquet except names starting 'rowmap_' or '_'); rowmaps auto-discovered from protected_dir.glob('rowmap_*.csv') with table = stem[len('rowmap_'):] (explicit rowmaps dict wins via setdefault); writes <out_dir or protected_dir>/scorecard.json (ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) and scorecard.html; returns the report dict. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:286-323; toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:52-65)_
- **Top-level report JSON structure**: {tool:'pets-eval 1.0.0', dataset, scenario (full scenario dict or null), original, protected, tables:{<table>:{...}}, extra_protected_files:[tables in protected not in original], utility:[{id,table,kind,description,required,score,metric,detail}], summary:{privacy,utility,composite,label,method}, risk_components:{'<table>: <risk name>': float}}. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:301-318; results/b0/customer_service/scorecard.json:1-488)_
- **Table status branch: withheld / error / released**: For each ORIGINAL table t: if t not in protected tables -> {table, status:'withheld', rows_original}; if evaluate_table raises -> {table, status:'error', error, trace}; else status:'released' with full metrics. Tables present only in protected go to extra_protected_files and are not evaluated. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:304-315)_
- **Per-table report fields (released)**: table, status, rows_original, rows_protected, columns_dropped, columns_added, direct_identifiers_retained {col: share}, [hash_attack], k_anonymity {qis,n,n_classes,min_k,median_k,share_below{k<2,k<5,k<10},sample_uniqueness} or {note:'no catalogued quasi-identifier kept'}, k_anonymity_original, [l_diversity {evaluated,sensitive,qis,min_distinct_l,min_entropy_l,share_records_l1,share_classes_l1,n_classes}], [trajectory_unicity], row_alignment ('row map' | 'original record ids kept in the release (itself a linkage key)' | 'none'), linkage {<adversary>:{...} | note}, [free_text {<col>:{...}}], [synthetic {dcr, membership_inference}], regex_residuals {col:{LABEL:count}}, risks {name: float}, seconds. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:70-243)_
- **Record key resolution (what original_record_id is)**: io.record_key(catalog, domain, table, df): the catalog column with privacy_role=='record_key' if present in df, else first column ending in '_id' whose values are unique, else None. For customer_service: customers.customer_id, conversations.conversation_id, turns.turn_id are catalogued record_key (values like C000001, CNV-000001, T0000001). _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:158-168; metadata/field_catalog.csv:438,456,471; data/customer_service/*.csv headers)_
- **Rowmap file format**: rowmap_<table>.csv with columns protected_row (0-based row index in the protected CSV) and original_record_id. load_rowmap accepts column names protected_row|row|index|protected_index (else first column) and original_record_id|record_id|original_id (else last column); protected_row coerced to numeric Int64, rows with NaN dropped. It is used only for scoring, never publish. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:8-9; toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:146-155)_
- **How baselines produce rowmaps**: write_protected(tables, originals, out_dir, cat, domain): writes out_dir/<t>.csv (index=False) and, when record_key rk exists in the original and len(orig)==len(protected), writes out_dir/rowmap_<t>.csv as DataFrame({'protected_row': range(len(df)), 'original_record_id': o[rk].astype(str).values}). Row order is preserved by the baselines, so protected row i maps to original row i. quickstart does the same for ed_visits using visits.visit_id. _(baselines/_common.py:139-148; examples/quickstart.py:48-51)_
- **Row-level vs synthetic classification branch**: _record_ids_for_rows: if rowmap given -> ('row map'); elif record_key column kept in protected and >50% of its values are in the original id set -> synthesised rowmap from protected[rk] with source 'original record ids kept in the release (itself a linkage key)'; else None/'none'. When rm is None: 'records with k<5' is popped from risks and k_anonymity.note set to 'not scored as a risk: rows are not linked to real records (synthetic or aggregate)'; linkage = {note:'no row map: linkage not evaluated (treated as synthetic / aggregate release)'}; free_text columns get {evaluated:false, reason:'needs a row map to align texts'}; synthetic block (DCR, membership inference vs holdout/) runs on non-identifier columns with nunique < 0.5*len(orig). _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:58-67, 132-137, 185-186, 202-204, 215-230)_
- **Risk 1: direct identifiers retained**: For each catalogued direct_identifier column present in both orig and prot: share = fraction of protected values (normalised: strip, lower, remove whitespace/-/.) that are in the set of original values; recorded only if >0; risk 'direct identifiers retained' = max share (0.0 if none). Dropping or tokenising the column yields 0. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:42-43, 78-88)_
- **Risk 2: hashed ids reversible**: attacks.detect_hash_columns(prot) (min_share 0.9 hash-looking values) -> for each, hash_dictionary_attack against up to 300000 unique original direct/technical identifier values; risk 'hashed ids reversible' = max share_values_reversed. Keyed HMAC tokens are not reversible by this; unkeyed hashes are. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:90-98; toolkit/pets_eval/attacks.py:490,517)_
- **Risk 3: records with k<5**: qis = catalogued quasi_identifier columns still present in protected. If any: k_anonymity(prot, qis) and k_anonymity_original(orig, qis∩orig); risk 'records with k<5' = share_below['k<5']; l_diversity computed on first catalogued sensitive_attribute kept (customers: payment_default_flag). If no QI kept: k_anonymity = {note:'no catalogued quasi-identifier kept'} and no k risk. customer_service QIs: customers [postcode, city, preferred_language, customer_since]; conversations [language, started_ts]; turns [ts]. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:100-111; metadata/field_catalog.csv:443-448,461-462,475; results/b0/customer_service/scorecard.json:18-22,120-126,221-224)_
- **Risk 4: linkage re-identification (attack selection branches)**: Runs only if rm is not None AND truth/<domain>__<table>.csv exists with non-empty person_id. specs = attack_specs.attacks filtered to dataset+table. Branch A: no spec for this table but specs exist for the dataset -> plan=[] and linkage.note='no attack spec targets this table (metadata/attack_specs.json)' (customer_service conversations and turns). Branch B: specs exist -> adversaries chosen by _adversaries_for (names appearing in scenario.threat_model text if scenario given, else names containing domain prefix e.g. 'customer', else all with truth). Branch C: dataset has no specs at all -> auto QI mapping per adversary. For each: if spec and no spec QI column survives in protected -> {evaluated:true, qis_used:[], reidentification_rate:0.0, n_targets_in_data:null, note:'every attacker column this attack needs was removed from the release'}; else attacks.linkage_attack(...). Baseline on original computed -> baseline_reidentification_rate_original and risk_reduction. risk 'linkage re-identification' = max over adversaries of max(reidentification_rate, attribute_inference.advantage_over_base_rate). Exceptions -> {evaluated:false, reason:'error: ...'}. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:46-55, 130-186)_
- **customer_service attack spec**: Only one spec: adversary 'leaked_customer_list', table customers, sensitive accessibility_needs, qis: name(name->full_name), exact(email->email), exact(city->city). adversary/leaked_customer_list.csv has 2600 rows with columns adv_row_id,name,email,phone,city,interest,list_year; truth/adversary__leaked_customer_list.csv maps adv_row_id->person_id. In all baselines only the city QI survives (qis_used=[city]), n_adversary_rows_tested 2600, n_targets_in_data 2345, reidentification_rate 0.0, baseline_reidentification_rate_original 0.8392, risk_reduction 1.0, attribute_inference success_rate 0.0013 / base rate 0.0162. _(metadata/attack_specs.json (attacks entry for customer_service); adversary/leaked_customer_list.csv header; results/b0/customer_service/scorecard.json:172-204)_
- **Linkage attack sampling limit and outputs**: linkage_attack(adversary, adv_truth, protected, rowmap, identity, qis=None, original=None, record_key=None, sensitive=None, temporal_cols=(), max_adversary=3000, seed=0, entity=None) -> dict; if len(adversary) > max_adversary it samples max_adversary rows uniformly with np.random.default_rng(seed). Returns evaluated, qis_used, n_adversary_rows_tested, n_targets_in_data, reidentification_rate, claim_precision, n_unique_claims, share_targets_in_candidate_set_le5, median_candidate_set, attribute_inference{sensitive,inferred,base_rate_majority_guess,advantage_over_base_rate,success_rate}; scorecard adds attack, baseline_reidentification_rate_original, risk_reduction. Not evaluated if no overlapping QIs ('no overlapping quasi-identifiers between adversary and protected table') or rowmap/adv_truth missing ('row map or adversary truth missing'). _(toolkit/pets_eval/attacks.py:389-426; results/b0/customer_service/scorecard.json:173-203)_
- **Risk 5: free-text identifier leakage**: For each catalogued free_text column (customer_service: conversations.agent_note, turns.text): gold = metadata/pii_spans/<domain>__<table>__<col>.jsonl; branches: no gold file -> {evaluated:false, reason:'no gold spans in package'}; column dropped -> {evaluated:true, status:'withheld', identifying_leakage_rate:0.0}; no rowmap -> {evaluated:false, reason:'needs a row map to align texts'}; else texts = {original_record_id: prot[col][protected_row]} and text.redaction_leakage(gold, texts). Risk 'free-text identifier leakage' = max identifying_leakage_rate over text columns. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:188-213; toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:91-92)_
- **redaction_leakage scoring details**: redaction_leakage(gold, protected_texts, labels=None, original_texts=None): records absent from protected_texts are skipped (treated as withheld). Protected text and gold value normalised by lowercasing and removing [\s\-\.\(\)/_:]+; PHONE adds digit-only, 358<->0 variants; values with normalised length <3 skipped; leaked if any variant is a substring of the normalised protected text. Output: leakage_rate (count), leakage_rate_chars, identifying_leakage_rate (labels in IDENTIFYING = PERSON, NATIONAL_ID, EMAIL, PHONE, ADDRESS, IBAN, PAYMENT_CARD, ACCOUNT_NUMBER, IP_ADDRESS, LICENSE_PLATE, USERNAME, SECRET, DEVICE_ID, PROPERTY_ID, URL; HEALTH/LOCATION/DATE/ORG/AGE excluded), per_label {label:{n,leaked,rate}}, n_values, examples (popped by scorecard). _(toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:19-21, 77-146; toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:208-209)_
- **Gold span files for customer_service**: metadata/pii_spans/customer_service__conversations__agent_note.jsonl (8981 lines) and customer_service__turns__text.jsonl (39416 lines); each line {record_id, spans:[{start,end,label,text}]}; record_id is conversation_id (CNV-xxxxxx) / turn_id (Txxxxxxx). Only split=='train' conversations are labelled (eval labels held by organisers). Scorecard denominators for customer_service: agent_note n_values 16751 (ACCOUNT_NUMBER 4712, HEALTH 227, NATIONAL_ID 2460, PERSON 8980, PHONE 372); turns.text n_values 48058 across 19 labels (PERSON 19843, NATIONAL_ID 5120, PHONE 4217, ACCOUNT_NUMBER 3967, DATE 2837, ADDRESS 2388, EMAIL 1999, IBAN 1473, ORG 1351, LOCATION 1281, PAYMENT_CARD 856, HEALTH 700, DEVICE_ID 572, SECRET 466, URL 440, IP_ADDRESS 356, PROPERTY_ID 103, USERNAME 62, LICENSE_PLATE 27). Other pii_spans files: cyber__incident_tickets__description, education__counsellor_notes__note_text, energy__customers__dso_notes, finance__transfers__message, health__clinical_notes__note_text, health__ed_visits__chief_complaint, public_admin__service_requests__description, public_admin__service_requests__response_text. _(ls metadata/pii_spans; head of jsonl files; data/customer_service/README.md; results/b0/customer_service/scorecard.json:54-89,255-359)_
- **Residual identifier regex scan (step 7)**: On prot.head(20000), every non-numeric/non-bool column is joined with newlines and scanned by check.scan_text; patterns NATIONAL_ID (HETU checksum validated), IBAN (mod-97), PAYMENT_CARD (Luhn + IIN prefix; dates and 18-digit 643* GSRNs skipped; 15-digit 35/86/01 relabelled IMEI), EMAIL, PHONE (Finnish +358/00358/0 + 4x/50 mobile), IP_ADDRESS, IPV6, MAC_ADDRESS, LICENSE_PLATE. Result in regex_residuals {col:{LABEL:count}}; it is informational, NOT added to risks (run_all.summarise's 'residual_identifiers' picks risk keys containing 'residual' or 'direct', i.e. 'direct identifiers retained'). B0 turns.text residuals: NATIONAL_ID 379, IBAN 145, PAYMENT_CARD 77, IMEI 52, EMAIL 186, PHONE 547, IP_ADDRESS 54, LICENSE_PLATE 1; B2 turns.text PHONE 4. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:232-240; toolkit/pets_eval/check.py:17-102; baselines/run_all.py:30-37; results/b0/customer_service/scorecard.json:361-372; results/b2/customer_service/scorecard.json:359-363)_
- **Utility task selection and 'required' flag**: run_utility: tasks = domain's TASKS; if a scenario is given, selected = tasks whose id is in scenario.utility_requirements or whose scenarios list contains the scenario id (fallback: all tasks); required = id in utility_requirements, or True for every task when no scenario (baselines ran with scenario=None so all 7 are required). Task exceptions -> {score:null, metric:'error', detail:{error, trace}}. Task fn signature fn(orig: dict[str,DataFrame], prot: dict[str,DataFrame]) -> {score, metric, detail}; score clamped to [0,1]; not_answerable(missing) -> {score:null, metric:'not answerable', detail:{missing:[...]}}. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:246-261; toolkit/pets_eval/utility/__init__.py:21-55)_
- **customer_service utility tasks (columns needed)**: CS-U1 (turns, model, scenarios CS-S1/CS-S2): needs prot turns[conversation_id,text] and prot conversations[conversation_id,intent]; trains TF-IDF+LogReg on protected train docs (turns grouped by conversation_id, train split from prot.split or original split mapped via conversation_id), tests on original eval docs; score = macroF1_protected/macroF1_original; not_answerable(['train conversations']) if fewer than 50 protected train conversations assemble (join via conversation_id). CS-U2 (conversations, relationship, CS-S2): sentiment,csat -> 1-|Δ Spearman|/0.5. CS-U3 (distribution, CS-S1): intent -> 1-2·TVD. CS-U4 (aggregate, CS-S1/S3): intent,handle_time_s -> mean by intent MAPE, 0.5->0. CS-U5 (turns, text, CS-S1/S2): turn_id,text -> share of common tokens (regex [a-zåäöéü]{3,}, appearing in >=25 conversations) retained, matched by turn_id on a 20000-turn sample (random_state=7). CS-U6 (aggregate, CS-S3): channel,language counts MAPE. CS-U7 (aggregate, CS-S3): intent,resolved -> FCR rate by intent, mean abs diff, 0.2->0. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:106-242)_
- **Scenario utility requirements for customer_service**: CS-S1 (external LLM analytics vendor): utility_requirements [CS-U1, CS-U3, CS-U5, CS-U4]; threat model names leaked_customer_list.csv; targets: no residual direct identifiers in text (recall >=0.98 on NATIONAL_ID, PAYMENT_CARD, IBAN, SECRET), remove HEALTH, consistent pseudonyms within a conversation, round timestamps to hour. CS-S2 (internal intent model): [CS-U1, CS-U2, CS-U5]. CS-S3 (BPO quality audit): [CS-U4, CS-U6, CS-U7]; suggests dropping customer_id and generalising started_ts to week. scenarios.json has 27 scenarios total. _(metadata/scenarios.json entries CS-S1..CS-S3)_
- **Composite scoring**: privacy = 1 - (0.5*max(risks) + 0.5*mean(risks)) over all 'table: risk' components (None if no risks); utility = mean over required tasks (null -> 0.0) plus optional tasks with non-null score; composite = (30+25)/(30/p + 25/u) weighted harmonic mean, 0 if either <=0. Labelled 'self-assessment, not the official judging score'. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:33, 264-283)_
- **Baseline scripts that handle customer_service**: grep -l customer_service baselines/*.py matches only run_all.py (DOMAINS list line 22). protect.py is generic: `python3 baselines/protect.py --level {b0,b2,b2k} --dataset customer_service [--scenario CS-S1] [--out results/b2/customer_service]`; it loads catalog_for(dataset), io.load_tables(ROOT/data/dataset), protect_table per table, rmtree(out), write_protected, run_scorecard(ROOT/data/dataset, out, scenario, root=ROOT, out_dir=out). run_all.py: `python3 baselines/run_all.py [--domains a,b]` runs B1 detection then b0/b2/b2k for each domain, writes results/benchmark.json and results/b1_field_labels.csv; its summarise() extracts privacy/utility/composite, worst_reid (max risk key containing 'reid' or 'linkage'), residual_identifiers (max key containing 'residual' or 'direct'), utility_tasks; per_scenario() = mean of each scenario's required task scores (null=0). _(baselines/run_all.py:22-114; baselines/protect.py:1-29; grep output)_
- **Baseline protect_table transformation rules**: Catalog-driven (baselines read field_catalog, i.e. they cheat on detection). b0: drop direct_identifier columns, keep everything else. b2: direct_identifier with subtype in TOKEN_SUBTYPES {NATIONAL_ID, IBAN, PAYMENT_CARD, LICENSE_PLATE, CUSTOMER_ID, ACCOUNT_ID, EMPLOYEE_ID, STUDENT_ID, PATIENT_ID, CARD_ID, DEVICE_ID, MAC_ADDRESS, IMEI, HOSTNAME, USERNAME, METER_ID, PROPERTY_ID} -> HMAC-SHA256 token 't_'+hex[:16] (key b'baseline-demo-key-rotate-me'), other direct identifiers (PERSON_NAME, EMAIL, PHONE, STREET_ADDRESS...) dropped; technical_identifier -> prefix-preserving IPv4 or HMAC token; quasi_identifier -> generalise (BIRTH_DATE->year, AGE->band, POSTCODE->3-digit prefix+'**', GPS->round 2, TIMESTAMP->floor hour 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:00', DATE->'YYYY-MM-DD', else unchanged); free_text -> regex_redact; record_key, sensitive_attribute, non_sensitive untouched. b2k: b2 then enforce_k(qis, 5) local suppression (blank most-detailed QI of rows in classes <5, iterate). Columns not in catalog are passed through. _(baselines/_common.py:21-27, 63-66, 74-136)_
- **Baseline text redaction and spans**: regex_redact replaces matches in order NATIONAL_ID, EMAIL, IBAN, URL, PAYMENT_CARD, PHONE, IP_ADDRESS, MAC, LICENSE_PLATE with literal '[LABEL]' placeholders; no PERSON/ADDRESS/HEALTH/ACCOUNT_NUMBER/SECRET handling; baselines emit NO span files (nothing writes JSONL); scoring uses redaction_leakage on text only. quickstart's chief_complaint redaction likewise is a single re.sub to '[ID]'. text.spans_from_redaction(original, protected) exists to recover 'ANY' spans by difflib if needed for span_scores. _(baselines/_common.py:42-60; examples/quickstart.py:45-46; toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:149-158)_
- **Effect of baseline tokenisation on customer_service**: B0 customers columns_dropped: customer_number, full_name, hetu, street_address, email, phone, contract_number, iban; conversations drops agent_name; turns drops nothing. B2 customers drops only full_name, street_address, email, phone (customer_number/hetu/contract_number/iban tokenised, note regex_residuals flags 1 PAYMENT_CARD-looking token in hetu and contract_number); conversations.customer_id/agent_id and turns.conversation_id become HMAC tokens while conversations.conversation_id (record_key) stays raw -> CS-U1 'not answerable' missing ['train conversations'] in B2/B2K. _(results/b0/customer_service/scorecard.json:13-15,108-117,218; results/b2/customer_service/scorecard.json:103-108,196-203,374-386; baselines/_common.py:110-116; toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:122-125)_
- **Reference scorecard numbers customer_service**: B0: privacy 0.2222, utility 1.0, composite 0.3438; risks conversations k<5 1.0 / leakage 1.0, customers k<5 1.0 / linkage 0.0, turns k<5 1.0 / leakage 1.0; all utility 1.0. B2: privacy 0.3126, utility 0.8557, composite 0.4394; conversations k<5 0.7237, agent_note identifying leakage 0.8286 (NATIONAL_ID 0, PHONE 0, PERSON/ACCOUNT_NUMBER/HEALTH 1.0); turns k<5 0.0188, text identifying leakage 0.8012 (IP 0, URL 0, IBAN .2566, DEVICE_ID .2832, PHONE .3275, USERNAME .5, EMAIL .5363, PAYMENT_CARD .5491, NATIONAL_ID .6412, LICENSE_PLATE .6667, PERSON/ADDRESS/ACCOUNT_NUMBER/SECRET/PROPERTY_ID 1.0); CS-U1 null, CS-U5 0.9899. B2K: privacy 0.4952, utility 0.8557, composite 0.6125; all k<5 risks 0.0 (min_k 5), leakage unchanged. benchmark.json utility_by_scenario B2/B2K: CS-S1 0.748, CS-S2 0.663, CS-S3 1.0; runtimes 20-29 s. _(results/b0|b2|b2k/customer_service/scorecard.json summary and risk_components; results/benchmark.json baselines B0_/B2_/B2K_customer_service)_
- **Truth files for customer_service**: truth/customer_service__customers.csv (9591 rows), __conversations.csv (11943), __turns.csv (140345), all with header record_id,person_id (e.g. CNV-000001,P000010; C000001,P000010; T0000001,P000010). identity truth is loaded by table; linkage requires rowmap.original_record_id values to equal these record_ids. _(truth/ listing and head; toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:136-138; toolkit/pets_eval/attacks.py:412-419)_
- **Original customer_service table columns**: customers.csv: customer_id,customer_number,full_name,hetu,street_address,postcode,city,email,phone,preferred_language,customer_since,products,contract_number,payment_method,iban,marketing_consent,payment_default_flag,accessibility_needs (9591 rows). conversations.csv: conversation_id,customer_id,agent_id,agent_name,channel,language,started_ts,intent,sentiment,csat,resolved,handle_time_s,n_turns,split,agent_note (11943). turns.csv: turn_id,conversation_id,seq,speaker,ts,text (140345). _(data/customer_service/*.csv headers; data/customer_service/README.md)_
- **CSV reading dtype behaviour**: io.read_table forces str dtype on columns whose name matches _STRINGY (id, hetu, postcode, phone, iban, card, plate, number, account, code, ...), all others via pandas inference with keep_default_na=True. Protected CSVs must keep original column names; generalised values accepted by pets_eval.parse: age bands '30-39'/'90+', truncated postcodes '201**', rounded times, '2025-03', '2025-W12'. _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:24-49; toolkit/README.md:19-21)_
- **results/ contents**: results/ holds b0/, b2/, b2k/ (each with the 9 domains incl. customer_service, only scorecard.html + scorecard.json), b4/health, b1_field_labels.csv, benchmark.json (generated 2026-11-04 09:46). No protected CSVs or rowmap files are shipped; scorecard paths reference /home/claude/trusted/dist/... from the organisers' run. _(ls -R results; results/*/customer_service/scorecard.json lines 5-6)_
- **quickstart.py (health example of a minimal staging folder)**: Writes results/quickstart/health/ed_visits.csv with a subset of columns (visit_id kept raw as row key, patient_hetu -> HMAC pseudonym in NEW column patient_pseudonym, age band, hourly arrival_ts, ICD-10 truncated, naive regex redaction of chief_complaint) plus rowmap_ed_visits.csv {protected_row: range(len(p)), original_record_id: visits.visit_id}; then run_scorecard(ROOT/'data'/'health', OUT, scenario='HEALTH-S1', root=ROOT) and prints rep['summary'] and per-task id/score/description. _(examples/quickstart.py:33-59)_

Gotchas:
- Table status in the report is only 'released' | 'withheld' | 'error'; there is no per-test 'not_applicable'/'unsupported' status. The adapter must derive those from branch markers: linkage.note strings, free_text[col].evaluated=false + reason, k_anonymity.note, utility metric 'not answerable' with detail.missing, utility metric 'error'.
- A table counts as row-level only if a rowmap_<table>.csv is present (or the raw record_key ids survive in the protected CSV, which is itself reported as a linkage key). Without it the toolkit silently reclassifies the table as synthetic: k<5 is not scored, linkage is skipped, free-text leakage is NOT evaluated ('needs a row map to align texts'), and DCR/membership inference run instead.
- rowmap.original_record_id must be the exact record_key value string of the original row (customer_id / conversation_id / turn_id), because truth/<domain>__<table>.csv and the gold span JSONL are keyed by those ids. protected_row is a 0-based index into the protected CSV as written (after any row reordering/suppression/sampling); rows out of range are ignored.
- Keep the original file names (customers.csv, conversations.csv, turns.csv) and original column names for kept columns; a renamed column is reported as dropped+added and ignored by every metric. New columns (e.g. patient_pseudonym) are allowed and listed in columns_added. Files named rowmap_* or starting with '_' are skipped as tables.
- Pseudonymising a foreign key on one table but not the matching key on the other breaks join-based utility: B2/B2K tokenise turns.conversation_id but leave conversations.conversation_id raw, so CS-U1 becomes 'not answerable' (missing ['train conversations'], needs >=50 joined train conversations). Apply the same keyed map to conversations.conversation_id and turns.conversation_id (and keep conversations.split or the ids resolvable to the original split).
- Free-text leakage is substring-based after normalisation (lowercase, separators [\s\-\.\(\)/_:] removed, phone 358/0 variants); surrogates that keep the digits in a different grouping still count as leaked, and 1-2 char values are skipped. identifying_leakage_rate ignores HEALTH/DATE/LOCATION/ORG/AGE, but scenario CS-S1 asks to remove HEALTH anyway.
- Baselines emit no span files; the scorecard never consumes predicted spans. Span-level scoring is only via `pets-eval text --gold ... --pred spans.jsonl` (format: one JSON per line {record_id, spans:[{start,end,label}]}).
- run_scorecard always writes scorecard.json and scorecard.html into out_dir (default: the protected folder itself), so a staging folder gets polluted with the report unless out_dir is set elsewhere. protect.py also rmtree()s its output folder before writing.
- Linkage attack samples at most max_adversary=3000 adversary rows (seed 0); customer_service's only adversary has 2600 rows so no sampling occurs there. CS-U5 samples 20000 turns with random_state=7. Regex residual scan looks only at prot.head(20000) rows.
- Without --scenario every task is 'required' and null scores count as 0 in utility; with --scenario only required/scenario-tagged tasks run (fallback to all if none match). Scenario adversary selection matches adversary names as substrings of the threat_model text (e.g. 'leaked_customer_list').
- The hash-reversal check enumerates original direct/technical identifier values against any column that looks hashed; keyed HMAC tokens pass, unkeyed sha256 of raw ids would be flagged as 'hashed ids reversible'.
- Scorecard JSON uses default=str and ensure_ascii=False; a scenario run embeds the full scenario dict under 'scenario' instead of the id string.
- Baselines 'cheat' by reading metadata/field_catalog.csv for roles; the catalog is also what the scorecard uses to pick direct identifiers, QIs, sensitive attributes and free-text columns, so a transformation that leaves a catalogued direct_identifier column with original values is scored as retained regardless of the tool's own detection.

Open questions:
- Official judging score: scorecard.summary is explicitly 'self-assessment, not the official judging score'; the files read do not define the official formula or the organisers' stronger attacker.
- How eval-split (split=='eval') text leakage is scored: those spans are held by organisers and are absent from the shipped pii_spans files, so the local scorecard only covers train conversations; not determinable from the package.
- Whether the organisers' evaluation accepts rowmaps for tables whose protected row count differs from the original (write_protected only writes a rowmap when len(orig)==len(protected), but load_rowmap/evaluate_table impose no such constraint).
- pets_eval.privacy (k_anonymity, l_diversity, dcr_report, membership_inference_auc, trajectory_unicity), pets_eval.parse (generalised-value parsing) and attacks._Prepared/auto_qi_map internals were not read in full; exact matching tolerances for generalised QIs (age bands, hour-rounded timestamps, postcode prefixes) are therefore not documented here.
- b1_detect_rules.py and detect.score_detection were only skimmed: the prediction CSV needs columns dataset,table,column and optionally privacy_role,subtype, but the full role/subtype vocabulary normalisation (_norm) was not read.
- results/*/customer_service contains no protected CSVs or rowmaps, so there is no shipped on-disk example of a scored staging folder; the only way to obtain one is to run baselines/protect.py --level b2 --dataset customer_service (writes results/b2/customer_service/{customers,conversations,turns}.csv + rowmap_*.csv + scorecard.*).

## Reader: attacks

The pets_eval toolkit (Python 3.10+, pandas/numpy/scipy/scikit-learn; no console script installed here, run as `PYTHONPATH=<root>/toolkit python3 -m pets_eval ...`) scores a "protected" folder against the original dataset folder. The single entry point an adapter needs is `pets-eval scorecard --original <root>/data/customer_service --protected <staging> [--rowmap rowmap_x.csv|table=path]... [--scenario CS-S1|CS-S2|CS-S3] [--root <root>] [--out <dir>] [--max-adversary 3000]`, or the Python call `scorecard.run_scorecard(original_dir, protected_dir, scenario=None, root=None, rowmaps=None, out_dir=None, max_adversary=3000) -> dict`, which writes scorecard.json + scorecard.html. Staging-folder contract: same table file names as the original (customers.csv, conversations.csv, turns.csv), same column names for kept columns, generalised values allowed, and one `rowmap_<table>.csv` per released microdata table with columns `protected_row` (0-based row index in the protected CSV) and `original_record_id` (value of the catalog record_key: customer_id / conversation_id / turn_id). Files starting with `rowmap_` or `_` are skipped as tables. Missing table => status "withheld". No rowmap AND record_key column removed/not matching original ids => table treated as synthetic (DCR + membership inference vs holdout/, k<5 reported but NOT scored, linkage NOT evaluated, free-text leakage NOT evaluated). Per table, evaluate_table computes risk components keyed by name: "direct identifiers retained", "hashed ids reversible", "records with k<5", "trajectory unicity (<user>)" (mobility/smart_city tables only; none for customer_service), "linkage re-identification", "free-text identifier leakage", "membership inference advantage", "exact copies of original rows". Each component appears in `tables.<t>.risks` only when it was evaluated; absence (not NaN/zero) is the "not applicable" signal, except linkage/hash/free-text which also carry explicit `evaluated: false` + `reason` dicts. Composite: privacy = 1 - (0.5*max risk + 0.5*mean risk) over all table risks; utility = mean task score where required-but-unanswerable (score None) counts as 0 and optional None is dropped; composite = weighted harmonic mean (30/25); any exception inside a table yields `status: "error"` with `error`/`trace` and the table contributes no risks; any exception inside a utility task yields `score: None, metric: "error"`. The customer_service linkage attack (metadata/attack_specs.json, adversary "leaked_customer_list", table customers, sensitive accessibility_needs) uses QIs name(name->full_name), exact(email->email), exact(city->city); each QI is dropped automatically when its protected column is absent; if all three are absent the result is a stub `{evaluated: true, qis_used: [], reidentification_rate: 0.0, n_targets_in_data: None, note: ...}`. Tokenised/hashed/placeholder values survive as non-matching strings (so they do not match the adversary and act as a constraint that excludes the row), while empty/masked values ("", "***", "xxx", "###", "?") act as wildcards that match anything. Re-identification denominator is the number of (sampled, max 3000 uniform) adversary rows whose truth person_id maps to some protected row via rowmap+truth; numerator is adversary rows whose candidate set is exactly size 1 and whose single candidate row is that person. Attribute inference counts in-data targets whose non-empty candidate set has one distinct protected sensitive value and that value is in the person's original set; reported with majority-guess base rate and advantage. Worst of reidentification_rate and attribute advantage feeds "linkage re-identification". Free-text leakage per catalogued free_text column (conversations.agent_note, turns.text) needs gold spans (metadata/pii_spans/customer_service__<table>__<col>.jsonl, train split only: 8,981 conversations / 39,416 turns) and the rowmap; score = identifying_leakage_rate = share of gold spans with IDENTIFYING labels whose normalised value (case, whitespace, separators stripped; phone +358/0 variants) still appears in the protected text of the same record; column dropped => 0.0; table withheld => not evaluated. Utility tasks CS-U1..CS-U7 are selected by scenario (required = scenario.utility_requirements; if the scenario mentions none, all tasks are required) and need specific columns (listed in facts); missing columns => `score: None, metric: "not answerable", detail.missing: [...]`.

- **CLI: scorecard command and flags**: `pets-eval scorecard --original DIR --protected DIR [--rowmap R]... [--scenario ID] [--root ROOT] [--out DIR] [--max-adversary N(default 3000)]`. --rowmap is repeatable and accepts either a path (table name derived from stem minus 'rowmap_') or 'table=path'; rowmap_<table>.csv files inside --protected are auto-detected. Prints `privacy X utility Y composite Z`, one `risk  NN.N%  <table>: <component>` line per risk component and one `util  score  ID  metric` line per task, then `wrote <out>/scorecard.json and <out>/scorecard.html`. --out defaults to the protected folder. _(toolkit/pets_eval/cli.py:26-44, 111-119)_
- **CLI: other commands**: `pets-eval check PATH [--max-lines N] [--out F]` regex-scans files/folders (.csv .json .jsonl .txt .md .tsv) for residual identifiers; `pets-eval text --gold SPANS.jsonl (--pred spans.jsonl | --protected file.csv --text-col COL (--id-col ID | --rowmap R)) [--out F]`; `pets-eval detect --pred labels.csv [--catalog] [--root] [--datasets a,b] [--out]`; `pets-eval tasks [--dataset D]`; `pets-eval scenarios [--dataset D] [--root]`. Program name is `pets-eval` via pyproject [project.scripts]; not installed on this machine, so use `PYTHONPATH=<root>/toolkit python3 -m pets_eval <cmd>` (verified working for `tasks --dataset customer_service`). _(toolkit/pets_eval/cli.py:62-147; toolkit/pyproject.toml:17-18; toolkit/pets_eval/__main__.py:1-3)_
- **Python API entry point**: `scorecard.run_scorecard(original_dir, protected_dir, scenario: Optional[str]=None, root=None, rowmaps: Optional[dict]=None, out_dir=None, max_adversary: int=3000) -> dict`. domain = original_dir.name. root auto-detected by io.find_package_root (walk up from original_dir; or $PETS_ROOT env) looking for metadata/ plus data/ or adversary/. rowmaps dict is {table: path}; rowmap_*.csv in protected_dir are added via setdefault (explicit arg wins). Writes out_dir/scorecard.json and scorecard.html (out_dir defaults to protected_dir) and returns the report dict. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:286-323; toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:28-39)_
- **Report JSON top-level structure**: {tool: 'pets-eval 1.0.0', dataset, scenario (full scenario dict or raw id string if unknown), original, protected, tables: {<table>: <table report>}, extra_protected_files: [names in protected but not original], utility: [task results], summary: {privacy, utility, composite, label, method}, risk_components: {'<table>: <component>': value}}. Table report for a missing table: {table, status:'withheld', rows_original}. Table report on exception: {table, status:'error', error:'<Type>: <msg>', trace}. Otherwise status:'released' with keys rows_original, rows_protected, columns_dropped, columns_added, direct_identifiers_retained, [hash_attack], k_anonymity, [k_anonymity_original], [l_diversity], [trajectory_unicity], row_alignment, [linkage], [free_text], [synthetic], regex_residuals, risks, seconds. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:70-76, 240-243, 301-318)_
- **Composite scoring**: composite(risks, utility): privacy = 1 - (0.5*max(risks) + 0.5*mean(risks)) over all non-None risk values across tables (None if no risks at all). utility = mean over [required tasks with None->0.0] + [optional tasks with non-None score]; None if no tasks. composite = (30+25)/(30/p + 25/u) with p,u floored at 1e-9; forced to 0.0 if privacy<=0 or utility<=0; None if either is None. Values rounded to 4 dp. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:33, 264-283)_
- **Table loading rules**: io.load_tables(folder) loads every *.csv and *.parquet sorted by name, keyed by file stem; skips stems starting with 'rowmap_' or '_'; returns {} if folder missing. read_table forces dtype=str for columns whose name matches the _STRINGY regex (id, ids, hetu, ssn, postcode, zip, phone, mobile, iban, pan, card, plate, gsrn, meter, mac, imei, ip, code, icd, number, no, account, msisdn, ref, reference, property as name segments, or ending _id / starting id_); everything else is pandas-inferred with keep_default_na=True (so empty cells become NaN). _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:23-25, 42-65)_
- **Rowmap file contract**: io.load_rowmap(path): CSV read with dtype=str; protected_row column = first of (protected_row, row, index, protected_index) case-insensitive else the FIRST column; original_record_id column = first of (original_record_id, record_id, original_id) else the LAST column. protected_row coerced to Int64 via pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce'); rows with NaN in either are dropped. Convention (docstring + baseline writer): protected_row is the 0-based row index in the protected CSV; original_record_id is the original table's record_key value. Baseline writes it only when len(orig)==len(prot), with protected_row=range(len(df)). _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:146-155; toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:5-10; baselines/_common.py:139-148)_
- **Record key resolution**: io.record_key(catalog, domain, table, df): first catalog column for that (dataset, table) with privacy_role == 'record_key' that exists in df; else the first column of df whose name ends with '_id' and is unique; else None. For customer_service: customers.customer_id, conversations.conversation_id, turns.turn_id are catalogued record_key. _(toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:158-168; metadata/field_catalog.csv:438, 456, 471)_
- **Row alignment fallback when no rowmap**: _record_ids_for_rows(prot, rowmap, rk, orig_ids): if a rowmap exists it is used (row_alignment='row map'). Else if the record_key column rk is still in the protected table and >50% of its string values are in the original id set, an implicit rowmap protected_row=arange(len(prot)), original_record_id=prot[rk] is built (row_alignment='original record ids kept in the release (itself a linkage key)'). Else (None, '') -> row_alignment='none' and the table is treated as synthetic. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:58-67, 132-133)_
- **Rowmap + truth -> person**: linkage_attack builds id_map from identity truth (truth/<domain>__<table>.csv, columns record_id,person_id; first two columns used positionally, dtype str, NaN->''). For each rowmap row (pr, rid) with 0<=pr<len(protected): row_person[pr]=id_map.get(rid,''), row_record[pr]=rid. persons_in = set of non-empty row_person. Adversary rows map adv_row_id (first column) -> person_id via truth/adversary__<name>.csv (first two columns); unmapped -> ''. in_data = adversary person_id in persons_in. Rowmap rows pointing outside the protected length or to unknown record ids silently contribute nothing. _(toolkit/pets_eval/attacks.py:411-422; toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:127-138)_
- **Truth and adversary files for customer_service**: truth/customer_service__customers.csv (9,591 data rows; header record_id,person_id; e.g. C000001,P000010), truth/customer_service__conversations.csv (11,943 rows; CNV-000001,P000010), truth/customer_service__turns.csv (140,345 rows; T0000001,P000010), truth/adversary__leaked_customer_list.csv (2,600 rows; header adv_row_id,person_id; CSLP00001,P020463). adversary/leaked_customer_list.csv (2,600 rows; header adv_row_id,name,email,phone,city,interest,list_year; 310 rows have empty email, 509 empty city, 0 empty name). 2,345 of the 2,600 adversary person_ids occur in the customers truth, i.e. ~90% are in-data targets before sampling. Holdout: holdout/customer_service/{customers.csv (539 rows), conversations.csv (675), turns.csv (9,306)} with the same headers as data/; holdout customer C000058 does NOT appear in data/customer_service/customers.csv nor in the customers truth (non-member records). _(truth/customer_service__*.csv headers; adversary/leaked_customer_list.csv header; holdout/customer_service/*.csv headers; counts computed with csv module)_
- **Original table headers (customer_service)**: customers.csv: customer_id,customer_number,full_name,hetu,street_address,postcode,city,email,phone,preferred_language,customer_since,products,contract_number,payment_method,iban,marketing_consent,payment_default_flag,accessibility_needs. conversations.csv: conversation_id,customer_id,agent_id,agent_name,channel,language,started_ts,intent,sentiment,csat,resolved,handle_time_s,n_turns,split,agent_note. turns.csv: turn_id,conversation_id,seq,speaker,ts,text. Data README states 9,591 / 11,943 / 140,345 rows (turns.csv has 163,303 physical lines because text fields contain newlines). _(data/customer_service/customers.csv:1; conversations.csv:1; turns.csv:1; data/customer_service/README.md:8-12)_
- **Field catalog roles for customer_service**: customers: customer_id=record_key; customer_number, full_name, hetu, street_address, email, phone, contract_number, iban = direct_identifier; postcode, city, preferred_language, customer_since = quasi_identifier; products, payment_method, marketing_consent = non_sensitive; payment_default_flag, accessibility_needs = sensitive_attribute (accessibility_needs art9=True). conversations: conversation_id=record_key; customer_id, agent_id = technical_identifier; agent_name = direct_identifier; language, started_ts = quasi_identifier; agent_note = free_text; channel,intent,sentiment,csat,resolved,handle_time_s,n_turns,split = non_sensitive. turns: turn_id=record_key; conversation_id=technical_identifier; ts=quasi_identifier; text=free_text; seq,speaker=non_sensitive. Catalog columns: dataset,table,column,privacy_role,data_kind,subtype,art9_special_category,description,traps. _(metadata/field_catalog.csv:1, 438-476)_
- **Risk 1: direct identifiers retained**: For every catalogued direct_identifier column present in BOTH orig and prot: share = fraction of protected non-null values whose normalised form (strip, lower, remove whitespace/-/.) is in the set of normalised original values of that column. Only columns with share>0 are reported in direct_identifiers_retained {col: share}. risks['direct identifiers retained'] = max share, or 0.0 if none retained (always present in risks). Dropped columns contribute nothing. Tokens/hashes/surrogates that never equal an original value score 0; a column kept verbatim scores ~1.0. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:42-43, 78-88)_
- **Risk 2: hashed ids reversible**: attacks.detect_hash_columns(prot): a column is 'hashed' if >=90% of its first 2000 non-null string values fully match a 32/40/64-char hex digest (md5/sha1/sha256). For each such column, hash_dictionary_attack(prot[c], candidates[:300000]) where candidates = unique original values of all catalogued direct_identifier + technical_identifier columns of that table (pooled across columns). Each candidate is hashed with variants (raw, strip, lower, upper, digits-only, +358/0 phone forms, whitespace-stripped) using every algorithm whose digest length appears; max 2,000,000 variant hashes. Returns {evaluated, n_hashes, n_reversed_distinct, share_values_reversed, algorithm, candidates_tried, examples}; {evaluated:false, reason:'no values'} if column empty. risks['hashed ids reversible'] = max share_values_reversed, only added when at least one hash-looking column exists. HMAC/keyed tokens or non-hex tokens are never detected as hashes. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:90-98; toolkit/pets_eval/attacks.py:487-542)_
- **Risk 3: records with k<5**: qis = catalogued quasi_identifier columns present in prot (customers: postcode, city, preferred_language, customer_since; conversations: language, started_ts; turns: ts). If any: k_anonymity(prot, qis) -> {qis, n, n_classes, min_k, median_k, share_below:{'k<2','k<5','k<10'}, sample_uniqueness}; missing values are their own class (astype(str)); risks['records with k<5'] = share_below['k<5']; also k_anonymity_original on orig and l_diversity(prot, qis, first catalogued sensitive_attribute present). If no QI kept: k_anonymity = {note:'no catalogued quasi-identifier kept'} and no risk entry. If the table has no row alignment (rm is None) the 'records with k<5' risk is popped and note 'not scored as a risk: rows are not linked to real records (synthetic or aggregate)' added. Generalised values (e.g. '201**', '2025-W12') are compared as plain strings here, so coarsening raises k. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:100-111, 134-137; toolkit/pets_eval/privacy.py:18-41, 48-70)_
- **Risk 3b: trajectory unicity**: Only for (dataset, table) pairs listed in attack_specs.json 'trajectories': mobility/taps, mobility/bike_trips, smart_city/wifi_probes, smart_city/anpr_parking. None for customer_service, so this component never appears for it. When applicable: privacy.trajectory_unicity(prot, user_col, time_col, lat_col, lon_col, place_col, p, temporal, spatial_m, n_users=1000) -> {evaluated, p, spatial_m, temporal, n_users_tested, unicity} ; if user column removed from prot -> {evaluated:true, unicity:0.0, note:'<user> removed: traces cannot be linked'}; if time column missing -> {evaluated:false, reason:'user or time column missing'}; no location -> {evaluated:false, reason:'no location column'}; no usable points -> evaluated:false; no user with >=p points -> {evaluated:true, unicity:0.0, n_users_tested:0}. risks['trajectory unicity (<user>)'] = unicity when evaluated. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:113-128; toolkit/pets_eval/privacy.py:256-297; metadata/attack_specs.json:547-590)_
- **Risk 4: linkage attack selection and gating**: Linkage runs only if rm (rowmap or implicit) is not None AND identity truth exists for the table AND it has at least one non-empty person_id. Specs filtered to dataset==domain and table==table. If none for this table but the domain has specs for other tables: linkage = {note:'no attack spec targets this table (metadata/attack_specs.json)'} and no risk entry (this is the case for customer_service conversations and turns: only customers is targeted). Adversaries chosen by _adversaries_for: names with a truth file whose name appears in json.dumps(scenario.threat_model) (CS-S1 mentions leaked_customer_list.csv -> picked; CS-S2 and CS-S3 mention none -> falls back to names containing 'customer' i.e. leaked_customer_list); specs whose adversary is in that list, else all specs. If rm is None: linkage = {note:'no row map: linkage not evaluated (treated as synthetic / aggregate release)'}. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:46-56, 131-153, 185-186; metadata/scenarios.json CS-S1/S2/S3 threat_model)_
- **Risk 4: linkage call and result shape**: Per adversary: sens_col = spec.sensitive ('accessibility_needs') if present in orig, else first catalogued sensitive_attribute. q_p = qis_from_spec(spec.qis, prot.columns) keeps only QIs whose protected column(s) exist (geo needs both). If spec exists and q_p is empty -> res = {evaluated:true, qis_used:[], reidentification_rate:0.0, n_targets_in_data:None, note:'every attacker column this attack needs was removed from the release'} (counts as evaluated, contributes 0 risk). Else res = attacks.linkage_attack(adv, truth, prot, rm, identity, qis=q_p, original=orig, record_key=rk, sensitive=sens_col, temporal_cols=<catalog temporal cols>, max_adversary, entity=spec.entity). res['attack'] = description. If evaluated and rk exists, a baseline run on the ORIGINAL table with q_o adds baseline_reidentification_rate_original and risk_reduction = 1 - rate/base (only if base>0). Exceptions -> {evaluated:false, reason:'error: ...'}. linkage = {<adversary name>: res}. risks['linkage re-identification'] = max over evaluated adversaries of max(reidentification_rate, attribute_inference.advantage_over_base_rate), added only if at least one adversary evaluated. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:154-184; toolkit/pets_eval/attacks.py:39-48)_
- **Linkage: function signature and early exits**: attacks.linkage_attack(adversary: DataFrame, adv_truth: Optional[DataFrame], protected: DataFrame, rowmap: Optional[DataFrame], identity: DataFrame, qis: Optional[list]=None, original: Optional[DataFrame]=None, record_key: Optional[str]=None, sensitive: Optional[str]=None, temporal_cols=(), max_adversary=3000, seed=0, entity: Optional[str]=None) -> dict. qis None -> auto_qi_map by column names; empty qis -> {evaluated:false, reason:'no overlapping quasi-identifiers between adversary and protected table'}; rowmap or adv_truth None -> {evaluated:false, reason:'row map or adversary truth missing'}. Adversary sampled uniformly without replacement to max_adversary rows (seed 0) if larger (2,600 < 3,000 so the full leaked list is used by default). protected.reset_index(drop=True) before matching, so rowmap protected_row refers to CSV row order. _(toolkit/pets_eval/attacks.py:389-427)_
- **Linkage: QI kind 'name' matching**: Protected side: all listed protected name columns joined with ' ' (NaN->''), tokenised: lowercase, non-word chars (except - and whitespace) -> space, split on whitespace/-, keep tokens len>=2; inverted index token->rows; has_name[r] = row has >=1 token. Adversary side: join adversary name columns, same tokenisation. If adversary has no tokens -> QI skipped (no constraint, not counted as used). Blocking key = longest adversary token; candidate rows = index[key]; a row matches only if EVERY adversary token is in the row's tokens OR (token len<=2 and some row token starts with its first char). mask &= matched | ~has_name, i.e. rows whose protected name is empty/removed-to-blank are wildcards and stay candidates; rows with a surrogate/other name are excluded. A placeholder like '[PERSON]' tokenises to 'person' (has_name true) and never matches -> row excluded. No diacritic folding; exact token equality. _(toolkit/pets_eval/attacks.py:73-75, 279-287, 294-313)_
- **Linkage: QI kind 'exact' (email, city) and 'sex'**: Protected values normalised by _norm_str: NaN->'', lowercase, strip, remove [whitespace - . ( ) / _ :], and any value consisting only of [* x # ?] becomes '' (masked). Factorised into codes; empty code = lut.get('', -9). Adversary value normalised by _norm_scalar the same way; if adversary value is None/NaN/'' or normalises to '' -> QI skipped (not a constraint). Match: mask &= (codes == code(adv)) | (codes == empty code), so protected rows with empty/masked value are wildcards; any other non-equal value (token, hash, surrogate email, different city) excludes the row. lut.get(a,-2) ensures an unseen adversary value matches nothing except empties. For customer_service this applies to email->email and city->city. _(toolkit/pets_eval/attacks.py:51-53, 62-64, 248-252, 321-328)_
- **Linkage: other QI kinds (postcode, age, time, number, suffix, geo)**: postcode: digits only; protected grouped by digit length L; adversary prefix a[:L] must equal; protected rows with zero digits ('201**' -> '201' has 3 digits so it matches by 3-digit prefix; fully masked '*****' -> wildcard) ; adversary empty -> skipped. age: protected interval from birth column (name contains birth/dob; 4-char year -> 1-year width; 7-char month; else day) or band regex '30-39', '[30,40)', '90+', '<5', exact number -> [a,a+1); adversary interval ± tol (default 1.0, spec tol overrides); mask &= lo<adv_hi & hi>adv_lo; unparsable protected -> [-1,200) wildcard. time: protected parsed by parse.to_datetime; width 366d for 'YYYY', 31d for 'YYYY-MM', 7d for 'YYYY-Wnn', 1d for 'YYYY-MM-DD', 0 otherwise; adversary window (hours before, after) from spec, +1 day on 'after' if adversary value has no hh:mm; default ±3h with time, (-1d,+2d) without; NaT protected -> wildcard. number: |x-a| <= max(|a|*tol(default .01), .01) or NaN wildcard. suffix: last tol(default 4) digits equality; protected shorter -> ''. geo: haversine <= tolerance(from decimal places, min 150m)+250m or NaN wildcard. _(toolkit/pets_eval/attacks.py:79-167, 253-278, 329-384)_
- **Linkage: success counting and denominators**: For each adversary row: (cand, used) = candidate rows and count of QIs that actually constrained; size = len(cand); if entity column given and all candidates share one non-empty entity value, size=1. If in_data: n_in += 1; sizes.append(size); if 0<size<=5 and the true person is among candidates: n_k5 += 1. If size==1 and used>0: n_claim += 1; if in_data and candidate (first 50) has row_person == target: n_correct += 1. Output: n_adversary_rows_tested = len(adv after sampling); n_targets_in_data = n_in; reidentification_rate = n_correct/n_in (0.0 if n_in==0); claim_precision = n_correct/n_claim (None if no claims); n_unique_claims; share_targets_in_candidate_set_le5 = n_k5/n_in; median_candidate_set = median of sizes among in-data targets (0 if none); qis_used list of {kind, adversary, protected}. Adversary rows for persons not in the data cannot count as correct but do count as false unique claims (lower precision). Note: with no used QIs (all adversary fields empty) size==n and nothing is claimed. _(toolkit/pets_eval/attacks.py:435-472)_
- **Linkage: attribute inference on the sensitive column**: Enabled only if sensitive given AND original passed AND sensitive in original AND sensitive in protected AND record_key given. sens_true = per person_id set of original sensitive values (via original[record_key] -> id_map). For each in-data adversary row with 0<size and used>0: vals = set of protected sensitive values over candidates (astype str, so NaN -> 'nan'); if exactly one distinct value: n_attr += 1 and n_attr_ok += 1 if that value is in the person's original set. success_rate = n_attr_ok/n_in; base_rate_majority_guess = share of in-data targets whose original set contains the most frequent protected value; advantage_over_base_rate = max(0, (succ-base)/(1-base)) (0 if base>=1). Reported under res['attribute_inference'] = {sensitive, inferred, base_rate_majority_guess, advantage_over_base_rate, success_rate}. If the sensitive column is dropped from the protected table, the block is absent. Replacing values with a constant (e.g. 'nan'/'') makes every candidate set homogeneous; it counts as a correct inference only if that string equals the original value (empty accessibility_needs is 'nan' in both for most rows, which would inflate success but the majority base rate cancels it in advantage). _(toolkit/pets_eval/attacks.py:429-434, 455-460, 473-482)_
- **customer_service attack spec (attack_specs.json)**: Top-level schema: {version:'1.0', description, attacks:[{adversary, dataset, table, [sensitive], [entity], description, qis:[{kind, adversary:[cols], protected:[cols], [window:[before_h, after_h]], [tol]}]}], trajectories:[{dataset, table, user, time, [place] | [lat, lon], p, temporal, [spatial_m], description}]}. The only customer_service entry (attacks[15]): adversary 'leaked_customer_list', dataset 'customer_service', table 'customers', sensitive 'accessibility_needs', description 'An old marketing list with names, emails, phones and cities.', qis = [name: ['name'] -> ['full_name']; exact: ['email'] -> ['email']; exact: ['city'] -> ['city']]. The adversary's phone, interest and list_year columns are NOT used by the spec (phone would be used only by auto_qi_map when no spec exists). No 'entity' for this attack. No trajectories for customer_service. _(metadata/attack_specs.json:1-4, 510-545, 547-590)_
- **Risk 5: free-text identifier leakage**: For each catalogued free_text column in orig (conversations.agent_note, turns.text): gold = io.load_spans(metadata/pii_spans/<domain>__<table>__<column>.jsonl) -> {record_id: [{start,end,label,text}]}; if file missing or empty -> {evaluated:false, reason:'no gold spans in package'}; if column not in prot -> {evaluated:true, status:'withheld', identifying_leakage_rate:0.0}; if no row alignment -> {evaluated:false, reason:'needs a row map to align texts'}; else texts = {original_record_id: prot[c] at protected_row} over valid rowmap rows, res = text.redaction_leakage(gold, texts) with 'examples' removed, stored as {evaluated:true, leakage_rate, leakage_rate_chars, identifying_leakage_rate, per_label:{label:{n,leaked,rate}}, n_values}. risks['free-text identifier leakage'] = max identifying_leakage_rate over evaluated columns. Gold spans exist only for split=='train' records (8,981 conversation notes; 39,416 turn lines); records absent from protected_texts (not in rowmap) are skipped entirely (treated as withheld, not as leaks), so the denominator is gold spans of records present in the rowmap. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:188-213; toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:91-108; toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:98-146; metadata/pii_spans listing)_
