- **redaction_leakage matching rule**: text.normalise(s) = lowercase and remove all runs of [whitespace - . ( ) / _ :]. A gold span leaks if any variant of its normalised value is a substring of the normalised protected text; variants add for PHONE: digits-only, +358<->0 prefix forms. Spans whose normalised value is <3 chars are skipped. IDENTIFYING labels = PERSON, NATIONAL_ID, EMAIL, PHONE, ADDRESS, IBAN, PAYMENT_CARD, ACCOUNT_NUMBER, IP_ADDRESS, LICENSE_PLATE, USERNAME, SECRET, DEVICE_ID, PROPERTY_ID, URL (DATE, LOCATION, ORG, HEALTH, AGE count in leakage_rate but not identifying_leakage_rate). Rates are count-based: leaked/n per label; 0.0 when denominator 0. Consequence for an adapter: a spoken-form gold value like '070889 streck 965 2' normalises to '070889streck9652' and only leaks if the same spoken form survives; a surrogate name never matches; a first name like 'oscar' leaks if it appears anywhere in the protected text of that record. _(toolkit/pets_eval/text.py:19-21, 77-96, 98-146; metadata/pii_spans/customer_service__turns__text.jsonl:1-3)_
- **Risk 6: synthetic (no row alignment only)**: If rm is None and prot non-empty: cols = protected columns also in orig, excluding catalogued direct_identifier/free_text/record_key/technical_identifier, and with orig nunique < 0.5*len(orig). hold = holdout/<domain>/<table>.csv if present. dcr_report(prot, orig, hold, cols) -> {evaluated, columns, n_synthetic, median_dcr_train, share_exact_copies, median_nndr, [median_dcr_holdout, share_closer_to_train, train_holdout_size_ratio]} (max 20,000 rows sampled, seed 0) or {evaluated:false, reason:'no shared columns'}; risks['exact copies of original rows'] = share_exact_copies. If holdout exists: membership_inference_auc(prot, orig, hold, cols) (max 5,000 each side, seed 0) -> {evaluated, columns, n_each, auc, advantage=max(0,2*auc-1)}; risks['membership inference advantage'] = advantage. Requires scikit-learn. Nothing is added when cols is empty. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:215-230; toolkit/pets_eval/privacy.py:198-252; toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:141-143)_
- **Risk 7: regex residual scan (reported, not scored)**: For the first 20,000 protected rows, every non-numeric/non-bool column's values are joined with newlines and scanned with check.scan_text; output regex_residuals = {column: {label: count}}. Labels: NATIONAL_ID (HETU regex + checksum), IBAN (mod-97), PAYMENT_CARD (13-19 digits, IIN prefix + Luhn; 15-digit 35/86/01 -> IMEI; dates and 18-digit 643* GSRN excluded), EMAIL, PHONE (Finnish +358/00358/0 4x|50 patterns, pattern-only), IP_ADDRESS, IPV6, MAC_ADDRESS, LICENSE_PLATE (pattern-only). This block is NOT added to risks, so it never affects the privacy score; the HTML table shows per-column totals. The standalone `pets-eval check PATH` scans files line by line and returns {files:{path:{label:count}}, totals, examples (masked), n_files_scanned, note}. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:232-240; toolkit/pets_eval/check.py:17-27, 75-102, 105-126)_
- **Utility task selection and result shape**: run_utility(domain, orig, prot, scenario): tasks = all customer_service tasks; if a scenario is given, keep tasks whose id is in scenario.utility_requirements OR whose task.scenarios list contains the scenario id (falls back to all tasks if that selection is empty); required = id in utility_requirements, or ALL tasks when the scenario lists none / no scenario. Each entry: {id, table, kind, description, required, score (float 0..1 clipped or None), metric (str), detail (dict)}; exceptions -> {score:None, metric:'error', detail:{error, trace}}; missing columns -> {score:None, metric:'not answerable', detail:{missing:[...]}}. Scenario requirements: CS-S1 = CS-U1, CS-U3, CS-U5, CS-U4; CS-S2 = CS-U1, CS-U2, CS-U5; CS-S3 = CS-U4, CS-U6, CS-U7. Task scenarios lists: U1 [S1,S2], U2 [S2], U3 [S1], U4 [S1,S3], U5 [S1,S2], U6 [S3], U7 [S3]. _(toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:246-261; toolkit/pets_eval/utility/__init__.py:21-44; toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:231-242; metadata/scenarios.json CS-S1..S3 utility_requirements)_
- **Utility task column requirements and metrics (customer_service)**: CS-U1 u1_intent: needs prot.turns[conversation_id,text] and prot.conversations[conversation_id,intent]; trains TF-IDF(1-2gram, min_df 2, 60k features)+LogReg on protected train docs (conversations whose split=='train' from prot.split if present else mapped from orig), tests on ORIGINAL eval docs; score = macroF1(protected)/macroF1(original); not_answerable(['train conversations']) if <50 protected train conversations; docs are turns joined per conversation_id ordered by seq, so turn rows must keep conversation_id and text. CS-U2 u2_sent_csat: needs conversations[sentiment,csat]; 1-|Δ Spearman(sentiment{neg0,neu1,pos2}, csat)|/0.5; 0.0 if protected rho is NaN (<=10 valid pairs). CS-U3 u3_intent_mix: needs [intent]; 1-2*TVD of intent counts. CS-U4 u4_aht: needs [intent,handle_time_s]; handle_time_s parsed with parse_numeric (ranges -> midpoint); score = 1 - MAPE/0.5 over per-intent mean. CS-U5 u5_vocab: needs turns[turn_id,text]; common vocab = tokens [a-zåäöéü]{3,} appearing in >=25 original conversations; on a 20,000-turn sample (random_state 7) share of common tokens retained in the protected text matched BY turn_id (so turn_id must be kept verbatim in protected turns or score ~0). CS-U6 u6_channel_lang: needs [channel,language]; 1 - MAPE/0.5 of channel×language counts. CS-U7 u7_resolution: needs [intent,resolved]; resolved truthy if str lower in {true,1,yes}; score = 1 - mean|Δ rate|/0.2, missing intents count as error 1. _(toolkit/pets_eval/utility/customer_service.py:90-229)_
- **Generalised value formats understood by parsers**: parse.parse_numeric: numbers (comma decimal ok), '10-20'/'[10,20)' -> midpoint, '90+' -> +5, '<5' -> 2.5, ''/nan/none/null/*/suppressed -> NaN. parse.to_datetime: ISO8601 fast path, 'YYYY-Wnn' -> Monday of that ISO week, 'YYYY' -> Jan 1, 'YYYY-MM' -> 1st, Finnish d.m.yyyy [klo hh:mm], else NaT. postcode_prefix keeps first n digits. These formats also drive the linkage interval logic (time width by string shape; age bands). _(toolkit/pets_eval/parse.py:1-9, 22-51, 74-106, 128-130; toolkit/pets_eval/attacks.py:149-159)_
- **Scenario file structure**: metadata/scenarios.json is a JSON list of 27 scenario dicts with keys id, dataset, title, recipient, purpose, trust_level, threat_model, legal_context, utility_requirements (list of task ids), suggested_privacy_targets, notes. io.get_scenario(id, root) returns the dict by id or None (then run_scorecard stores the raw id string under 'scenario' and no scenario-based task filtering happens: all tasks required). _(metadata/scenarios.json (parsed); toolkit/pets_eval/io.py:78-88; toolkit/pets_eval/scorecard.py:294, 301)_
- **Environment**: Local python3 has pandas 2.3.3, scikit-learn 1.9.0, scipy 1.17.1 (toolkit requires numpy>=1.24, pandas>=2.0, scipy>=1.10, scikit-learn>=1.2, python>=3.10). `pets-eval` console script is not on PATH; `cd <root> && PYTHONPATH=toolkit python3 -m pets_eval tasks --dataset customer_service` works. Tests (tests/test_toolkit.py) invoke it as `python -m pets_eval` with PYTHONPATH=<root>/toolkit. _(toolkit/pyproject.toml:11-15; tests/test_toolkit.py:209-211; local run)_

Gotchas:
- Row-order coupling: rowmap protected_row indexes the protected CSV after pandas read; multi-line free-text cells are fine (pandas handles quoting) but the adapter must write CSVs with proper quoting and compute protected_row from the DataFrame row index, not from physical line numbers (turns.csv has 163,303 lines for 140,345 rows).
- Empty/masked protected values are WILDCARDS in the linkage attack (name: no tokens; exact: '' or only [*x#?]; postcode: no digits; time/number/geo: NaN). Blanking QI columns does not shrink candidate sets; it widens them. Replacing with a non-matching surrogate/token excludes the row from candidate sets, which is the behaviour that drives re-identification to 0 but is also 'free' protection the official judge may not grant.
- A placeholder like '[PERSON]' or 'REDACTED' in full_name tokenises to a non-empty token, so has_name is true and the row is excluded from every adversary's candidate set (0 re-identification) — but '[PERSON]' in free text is also checked by redaction_leakage only via substring of the gold value, so placeholders are safe there too.
- Dropping all three spec QI columns (full_name, email, city) from customers yields an 'evaluated: true' stub with reidentification_rate 0.0 and n_targets_in_data None; it still counts as an evaluated linkage with risk 0.
- If the record_key column (customer_id / conversation_id / turn_id) is kept verbatim and no rowmap is supplied, the toolkit synthesises a rowmap from it and labels row_alignment 'original record ids kept in the release (itself a linkage key)'; if the key is tokenised and no rowmap is written, the table silently becomes 'synthetic' (no linkage, no free-text leakage, k<5 unscored, DCR/MIA run instead), which can look like a great privacy score for the wrong reason.
- CS-U5 matches protected turns to original turns BY turn_id value (pmap.get(tid)); if turn_id is pseudonymised in the protected turns table the score collapses to ~0 even though the rowmap exists. Likewise CS-U1 joins turns to conversations by conversation_id value, so conversation_id must be consistent between protected turns and protected conversations (pseudonymised consistently is fine) and split must be kept in protected conversations or derivable from original by the same conversation_id values (if conversation_id is pseudonymised AND split dropped, the mapping from original split fails and no train docs are found -> not answerable).
- Free-text leakage denominator is restricted to records that are both in the gold spans (train split only) AND present in the rowmap; withholding eval-split rows does not change the rate, and withholding the text column entirely scores 0.0 leakage while any task that needs text becomes not answerable.
- Scenario threat_model text selection: CS-S2 and CS-S3 do not mention leaked_customer_list, so _adversaries_for falls back to any adversary whose name contains 'customer' — still leaked_customer_list. With an unknown scenario id, all 7 tasks become required (None scores count as 0).
- attribute_inference compares protected sensitive values as strings; NaN becomes 'nan'. If accessibility_needs is mostly empty in both original and protected, homogeneous 'nan' candidate sets count as correct inferences, but base_rate_majority_guess is also 'nan', so advantage_over_base_rate stays ~0; success_rate alone is misleading.
- hash detection only triggers on 32/40/64-char hex strings covering >=90% of a column; HMAC with a prefix (e.g. 'cust_ab12...') or base32/uuid tokens are never tested, and the hashed-ids component simply does not appear.
- regex_residuals never enters the privacy score; only direct identifiers retained, hashed ids, k<5, trajectory unicity, linkage, free-text leakage, membership inference and exact copies do.
- Linkage baseline on the ORIGINAL table is run for every adversary when a record key exists; with 2,600 adversary rows and 9,591 customers this is cheap, but each run tokenises names for all rows; max_adversary applies to both runs.
- zsh note for shell adapters: a shell word starting with '=' triggers zsh =command expansion; quote such strings when invoking from zsh.

Open questions:
- The official judging score is explicitly stated to differ ('organisers may evaluate with a different, stronger attacker'; scorecard is self-assessment); the files do not specify the private evaluation's adversary, QIs, or how eval-split free text (labels held by organisers) is scored.
- attack_specs.json has no entry for conversations or turns, so no linkage attack is ever run on those tables (only a note is emitted). Whether the organisers' private attacks target conversations via customer_id/started_ts (as CS-S3 threat_model suggests) is not in the files.
- No documented 'not_applicable' vs 'unsupported' vs 'failed' vocabulary exists in the toolkit; the adapter must derive it from (a) absence of a risk key, (b) 'evaluated: false' + reason, (c) 'status: withheld/error', (d) utility 'metric: not answerable' vs 'metric: error'. Mapping choices are up to the adapter.
- Sampling limits found: max_adversary 3000 (CLI flag), hash candidates 300,000 values / 2,000,000 variants, regex scan first 20,000 rows, detect_hash_columns first 2,000 values, DCR 20,000 rows, MIA 5,000 per side, trajectory 1,000 users, CS-U5 20,000-turn sample. No limit on linkage over the protected table itself; performance on 140k-row turns with k-anonymity on 'ts' (hash of strings) is untested here.
- Whether the protected folder may contain parquet instead of CSV for large tables is supported by read_table, but rowmaps are CSV-only (load_rowmap uses pd.read_csv).
- holdout/customer_service rows are disjoint from data/ (verified for one id); they are used only in the synthetic branch (no rowmap). Whether the organisers also use holdout for membership inference on rowmapped releases is not stated.
- Rowmap rows may legitimately omit protected rows (suppressed/withheld) or omit original ids (synthetic rows); linkage/free-text simply skip them, but k-anonymity still counts all protected rows. The intended treatment of partially mapped tables is not documented beyond this behaviour.
